category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The [___] cells, also known as Kulchitsky cells, are found scattered in the gastrointestinal mucosa and exhibit a high affinity for chromium salts.
back:
Enterochromaffin (EC) cells.
- Part of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES).
- Primary producer of Serotonin (5-HT).
- Involved in regulating gut motility.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient presents with chronic flushing, diarrhea, and wheezing. Lab tests show elevated 5-HIAA in urine, suggesting a tumor of which specific enteroendocrine cell?
back:
Enterochromaffin (EC) cells (Carcinoid Tumor).
- Secretes excess Serotonin.
- Located primarily in the ileum or appendix.
- Causes systemic 'Carcinoid Syndrome'.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which I-cells in the duodenum facilitate fat digestion upon the entry of chyme.
back:
Secretion of Cholecystokinin (CCK).
- Stimulates gallbladder contraction to release bile.
- Induces pancreatic enzyme secretion.
- Relaxes the Sphincter of Oddi.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the physiological triggers and primary actions of S-cells versus G-cells.
back:
S-cells: Triggered by low pH; secretes Secretin to increase bicarbonate.
G-cells: Triggered by peptides/distension; secretes Gastrin to increase HCL.
- Location: S (Duodenum), G (Antrum).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Identify the 'universal inhibitor' hormone produced by D-cells and its effect on the gastrointestinal tract.
back:
Somatostatin.
- Inhibits release of Gastrin, CCK, and Secretin.
- Decreases gastric acid and pancreatic secretion.
- Reduces intestinal absorption and blood flow.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The acronym [___] describes the biochemical characteristic of certain enteroendocrine cells to synthesize biogenic amines from amino acid precursors.
back:
APUD (Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation).
- Includes cells like EC cells.
- Converts tryptophan to serotonin.
- Converts histidine to histamine.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A 40-year-old female presents with refractory peptic ulcers and extreme gastric acid hypersecretion. Which enteroendocrine cell is most likely hyperplastic?
back:
G-cells (Gastrinoma/Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome).
- Located in the Gastrinoma triangle (pancreas/duodenum).
- Causes massive Parietal cell hyperplasia.
- Leads to severe steatorrhea and ulceration.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Describe the endocrine response of K-cells to an oral glucose load compared to intravenous glucose.
back:
Incretin Effect (GIP secretion).
- Oral glucose stimulates K-cells to release GIP.
- GIP increases insulin secretion from Pancreatic Beta cells.
- Result: Higher insulin spike than IV glucose.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Distinguish between the anatomical location and hormone product of L-cells versus Mo-cells.
back:
L-cells: Located in Ileum/Colon; produce GLP-1 (Incretin).
Mo-cells: Located in Duodenum/Jejunum; produce Motilin.
- Motilin initiates Migrating Motor Complex (MMC).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Name the specific hormone produced by P/D1 cells in the stomach that regulates hunger and growth hormone release.
back:
Ghrelin.
- Produced in the stomach fundus.
- Stimulates appetite (orexigenic).
- Increases during fasting; decreases after meals.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Gastric carcinoid tumors arise from the neoplastic proliferation of [___] cells within the gastric mucosa.
back:
• Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells
• Derived from APUD lineage
• Stimulated primarily by gastrin
• Located in oxyntic mucosa

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A 55-year-old female with long-standing pernicious anemia and hypergastrinemia shows multiple small fundic polyps. Biopsy reveals uniform cells with 'salt and pepper' chromatin. Name the diagnosis.
back:
• Type 1 Gastric Carcinoid
• Associated with chronic atrophic gastritis
• Gastrin-dependent hyperplasia
• Generally benign and indolent

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain the role of chronic hypergastrinemia in the pathogenesis of gastric neuroendocrine tumors.
back:
• Gastrin exerts trophic effects
• Causes ECL cell hyperplasia
• Progresses to dysplasia and neoplasia
• Common in Type 1 and Type 2 tumors

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast Type 1 gastric carcinoids with Type 3 (sporadic) carcinoids regarding biological behavior and gastrin levels.
back:
• Type 1: Multiple polyps, gastrin-dependent, excellent prognosis
• Type 3: Solitary tumor, gastrin-independent, highly aggressive and metastatic

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Identify the primary immunohistochemical markers used to confirm the histological diagnosis of a gastric carcinoid tumor.
back:
• Chromogranin A
• Synaptophysin
• CD56 (Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule)
• NSE (Neuron Specific Enolase)

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: On light microscopy, neuroendocrine cells in gastric carcinoids are classically arranged in nests or trabeculae with a characteristic [___] nuclear chromatin pattern.
back:
• Salt and pepper chromatin
• Uniformly round to oval nuclei
• Minimal mitotic activity
• Scant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with a solitary gastric neuroendocrine tumor presents with sudden facial flushing, diarrhea, and wheezing. Explain the clinical significance of these findings.
back:
• Represents Carcinoid Syndrome
• Suggests hepatic metastasis
• Vasoactive substances bypass liver metabolism
• Serotonin is the primary mediator

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain why gastric carcinoids are considered part of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES).
back:
• Shared APUD capabilities
• Produce biogenic amines/hormones
• Secretory granules show silver affinity
• Histologically distinct from glandular epithelium

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast the histological arrangement of carcinoid cells with the structure of typical gastric adenocarcinoma.
back:
• Carcinoid: Uniform cells in nests, cords, or ribbons; no mucin
• Adenocarcinoma: Glandular formation, significant atypia, and mucin production

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Specify the most common gastric location for gastrin-dependent carcinoid tumors.
back:
• Gastric Body and Fundus
• Area contains oxyntic mucosa
• High concentration of ECL cells
• Site of chronic atrophic changes

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Gastric carcinoid tumors primarily originate from the [___] cells of the gastric mucosa, which are a part of the diffuse neuroendocrine system.
back:
• Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells.
• These cells normally secrete histamine.
• Growth is stimulated by gastrin.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A 50-year-old female with pernicious anemia and chronic atrophic gastritis is found to have multiple small, yellow-tinted polypoid nodules in the gastric fundus. Identify the underlying histological driver.
back:
• Type 1 Gastric Carcinoid.
• Driven by hypergastrinemia (secondary to achlorhydria).
• Characterized by ECL cell hyperplasia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain the characteristic nuclear appearance (Salt and Pepper chromatin) observed in gastric neuroendocrine tumor cells.
back:
• Uniformly small, round nuclei.
• Coarsely clumped or stippled chromatin.
• Minimal mitotic activity in low-grade lesions.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast the biological behavior and multiplicity of Type 1 versus Type 3 gastric carcinoid tumors.
back:
• Type 1: Multiple small polyps, benign course, associated with high gastrin.
• Type 3: Solitary large mass, highly aggressive/metastatic, independent of gastrin levels.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Identify the two most specific immunohistochemical (IHC) markers used to confirm a diagnosis of a gastric carcinoid tumor.
back:
• 1. Chromogranin A.
• 2. Synaptophysin.
• Both reflect the presence of neurosecretory granules.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Gastric carcinoids occurring in the context of Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome and MEN-1 are categorized as [___] Gastric Neuroendocrine Tumors.
back:
• Type 2.
• Associated with excessive gastrin from a gastrinoma.
• Often multiple but less aggressive than Type 3.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with a sporadic gastric tumor presents with sudden skin flushing and wheezing. Explain why this usually indicates hepatic metastasis.
back:
• Serotonin enters systemic circulation directly.
• Bypasses first-pass metabolism by the liver.
• Known as Carcinoid Syndrome.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Describe the organizational histological patterns typically seen in a well-differentiated gastric carcinoid.
back:
• Cords or ribbons of cells.
• Solid nests or clusters.
• Occasional pseudorosettes or acini-like structures.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Distinguish between the terms 'APUDoma' and 'Carcinoid' in the context of gastric neuroendocrine pathology.
back:
• APUDoma: Refers to the metabolic capability (Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation).
• Carcinoid: Older term for well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Name the specific neuroendocrine cell system that populates the gastric glands and acts as the progenitor for NETs.
back:
• Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES).
• Also called the Argentaffin or Kulchitsky cell system.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
coreConcept: Cell of origin for gastric carcinoid
front: Gastric carcinoid tumors originate from [___] cells located in the gastric mucosa.
back:
• Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells.
• Neuroendocrine in origin.
• Growth is often driven by chronic hypergastrinemia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with autoimmune atrophic gastritis and Vitamin B12 deficiency is found to have multiple small nodules in the gastric fundus. Identify the most likely histological diagnosis and the driving hormone.
back:
• Diagnosis: Type I Gastric Carcinoid.
• Driving Hormone: Gastrin.
• Pathophysiology: ECL cell hyperplasia due to lack of acid feedback.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain the role of gastrin in the development of Type I and Type II Gastric Carcinoids.
back:
• Gastrin exerts a trophic effect on ECL cells.
• Chronic hypergastrinemia induces ECL cell hyperplasia.
• Progression leads to dysplasia and eventually neuroendocrine tumor formation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast Type I and Type III gastric carcinoids regarding their association with gastrin and their metastatic potential.
back:
• Type I: Associated with hypergastrinemia; multiple small lesions; very low metastatic risk.
• Type III: Sporadic (normal gastrin); solitary large mass; highly aggressive and metastatic.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: List the immunohistochemical markers used to definitively confirm the neuroendocrine nature of a gastric carcinoid tumor.
back:
• Chromogranin A.
• Synaptophysin.
• CD56 (NCAM).
• Neuron-Specific Enolase (NSE).

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Microscopic examination of gastric carcinoid cells reveals a characteristic nuclear chromatin pattern described as [___].
back:
• Salt-and-pepper chromatin.
• Fine, granular clumping.
• Uniform, round-to-oval nuclei with inconspicuous nucleoli.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A 50-year-old male with a solitary 3cm gastric mass and normal serum gastrin levels presents with flushing and diarrhea. Describe the clinical significance of these symptoms in this patient.
back:
• Indicates Carcinoid Syndrome.
• Suggests Type III sporadic tumor.
• Implies hepatic metastasis (serotonin bypassing first-pass metabolism).

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Describe the varied architectural growth patterns observed in gastric carcinoid tumors under light microscopy.
back:
• Solid nests or islands.
• Trabecular or ribbon-like arrangements.
• Occasional glandular or rosette-like structures.
• Cells separated by delicate vascular stroma.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Distinguish between the sources of hypergastrinemia in Type I versus Type II Gastric Carcinoids.
back:
• Type I: G-cell hyperplasia (secondary to achlorhydria/atrophic gastritis).
• Type II: Gastrin-secreting tumor (Gastrinoma) associated with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome/MEN-1.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Specify the gross anatomical layer where gastric carcinoids typically appear and their visual color.
back:
• Layer: Submucosa or deep mucosa.
• Color: Yellow or tan nodules.
• Texture: Firm with intact overlying epithelium.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: The immunohistochemical marker typically used to identify the neurosecretory granules in Gastric Carcinoid Tumors is [___].
back:
• Chromogranin A
• Synaptophysin is also commonly used
• Markers confirm neuroendocrine origin.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A 55-year-old male with chronic autoimmune atrophic gastritis is found to have multiple small gastric polyps. Biopsy reveals nests of uniform cells with 'salt and pepper' nuclei. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Type I Gastric Carcinoid
• Most common type (70–80%)
• Associated with achlorhydria and hypergastrinemia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain the role of hypergastrinemia in the pathogenesis of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors in patients with Pernicious Anemia.
back:
• Parietal cell loss leads to achlorhydria
• Uninhibited G-cell gastrin release
• Chronic trophic stimulation of ECL cells
• Triggers ECL cell hyperplasia and neoplasia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast the clinical behavior and multiplicity of Type I vs. Type III Gastric Carcinoids.
back:
• Type I: Multiple, small, benign course, gastrin-dependent.
• Type III: Solitary, large (>2cm), sporadic, highly aggressive/metastatic.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Describe the characteristic 'salt and pepper' chromatin seen in the histological assessment of carcinoid tumors.
back:
• Finely clumped, speckled chromatin pattern
• Uniformly distributed throughout the nucleus
• Key feature of neuroendocrine differentiation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Gastric carcinoid tumors originate from the [___] cells of the diffuse neuroendocrine system (DNES) within the oxyntic mucosa.
back:
• Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells
• These cells normally secrete histamine
• Located primarily in the gastric fundus/body.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with a solitary sporadic gastric carcinoid presents with systemic flushing and wheezing. What must be present for this clinical manifestation to occur?
back:
• Hepatic metastasis
• Bypasses liver's first-pass metabolism
• Serotonin/vasoactive amines reach systemic circulation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: How do Type II Gastric Carcinoid tumors differ from Type I in their associated clinical syndrome?
back:
• Type II: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome (ZES)
• Often associated with MEN1
• Driven by gastrinoma-secreted gastrin.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Distinguish the microscopic growth patterns commonly seen in Gastric Carcinoids.
back:
• Solid nests or islands
• Trabecular (ribbon-like) cords
• Glandular or organoid arrangements
• Stroma is typically highly vascular.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Name the specific organelle visible on electron microscopy that diagnosticates a Gastric Carcinoid.
back:
• Dense-core granules
• Membrane-bound neurosecretory granules
• Contain hormones like serotonin or histamine.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The [___] cells, primarily located in the gastric antrum and duodenum, are the principal source of Gastrin, which stimulates parietal cell acid secretion.
back:
• G cells
• Found in gastric antral pits
• Stimulated by protein, peptides, and vagal input
• Acts to increase HCl and gastric motility.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A 45-year-old female presents with biliary colic after a fatty meal. The hormone responsible for gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion is produced by [___].
back:
• I cells
• Located in the Duodenum and Jejunum
• Secretes Cholecystokinin (CCK)
• Actions: Gallbladder contraction and slowing gastric emptying.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which S cells respond to the presence of acidic chyme in the duodenum.
back:
• Secrete Secretin
• Stimulates pancreatic duct cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid
• Neutralizes gastric acid
• Inhibits gastric acid secretion and motility.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the primary hormonal products and endocrine roles of K cells versus L cells in the intestinal mucosa.
back:
• K cells: Secrete GIP (Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Peptide); found in proximal small intestine
• L cells: Secrete GLP-1 and PYY; found in distal ileum/colon
• Both function as incretins to enhance insulin release.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Describe the physiological role and local signaling mode of D cells within the gastrointestinal tract.
back:
• Secrete Somatostatin
• Acts via paracrine inhibition
• Decreases Gastrin, Secretin, CCK, and HCl secretion
• Found in stomach, intestine, and pancreatic islets.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The [___] cells, also known as Kulchitsky cells, are part of the DNES and exhibit a high affinity for silver or chromium salts.
back:
• Enterochromaffin (EC) cells
• Primary product: Serotonin (5-HT)
• Distributed throughout the gut mucosa
• Stimulate gut motility and secretion via the enteric nervous system.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient with diabetic gastroparesis is prescribed Erythromycin. This drug is effective because it mimics the hormone [___], normally produced by Mo cells.
back:
• Motilin
• Produced by Mo cells (Duodenum/Jejunum)
• Actions: Initiates Migrating Motor Complex (MMC)
• Stimulates upper GI motility during fasting.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: How do 'Open-type' enteroendocrine cells differ from 'Closed-type' cells in their sensing mechanism?
back:
• Open-type: Apical surface reaches lumen; acts as chemoreceptor (e.g., sensing amino acids)
• Closed-type: Do not reach lumen; stimulated by neural or mechanical stretch signals.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the stimulus for and the biological effect of Ghrelin versus PYY (Peptide YY).
back:
• Ghrelin: Produced by P/D1 cells (stomach); stimulates hunger (orexigenic)
• PYY: Produced by L cells (ileum/colon); induces satiety (anorexigenic) after food intake.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The acronym APUD, characterizing many DNES and enteroendocrine cells, stands for [___].
back:
• Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation
• Ability to synthesize biogenic amines (e.g., Serotonin)
• Key feature of neuroendocrine signaling cells.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: The histological progenitor cells for gastric carcinoid tumors, located within the gastric pits of the fundus and body, are the [___] cells.
back: * Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells. * Part of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES). * Regulate acid secretion by releasing histamine.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with chronic atrophic gastritis and achlorhydria presents with multiple small yellow intramucosal nodules in the gastric body. Biopsy shows 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin. State the most likely diagnosis.
back: * Type 1 Gastric Carcinoid Tumor. * Driven by hypergastrinemia due to loss of acid feedback. * Generally benign and indolent.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain how chronic hypergastrinemia promotes the neoplastic transformation of enteroendocrine cells in the stomach.
back: * Gastrin exerts a trophic (growth-promoting) effect on ECL cells. * Leads to hyperplasia, followed by dysplasia. * Progression to neoplastic carcinoid tumor.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A solitary 4cm ulcerated gastric mass is found in a patient with normal serum gastrin levels. Contrast this finding with the typical presentation of Type 1 Gastric Carcinoids.
back: * Likely Type 3 Sporadic Carcinoid. * Solitary and larger (vs. multiple/small). * Aggressive and metastatic (vs. indolent). * Not associated with hypergastrinemia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Identify the two most specific immunohistochemical markers used to confirm the neuroendocrine nature of a gastric carcinoid tumor.
back: * Chromogranin A. * Synaptophysin. * These markers target proteins within neurosecretory granules.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Under light microscopy, the characteristic nuclear appearance of carcinoid tumor cells is described as [___] chromatin.
back: * Salt-and-pepper (speckled). * Represents uniform, finely clumped chromatin. * Typical of neuroendocrine differentiation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with MEN-1 and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (ZES) is found to have multiple gastric carcinoids. Identify the specific classification and its underlying driver.
back: * Type 2 Gastric Carcinoid. * Driven by secondary hypergastrinemia from a gastrinoma. * Associated with MEN-1 syndrome.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Describe the physiological prerequisite for a gastric carcinoid tumor to manifest as systemic Carcinoid Syndrome (flushing, diarrhea).
back: * Hepatic Metastasis. * Vasoactive substances (serotonin) must bypass hepatic first-pass metabolism. * Reaches systemic circulation via hepatic veins.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Distinguish between the typical growth patterns (architectural arrangements) seen in carcinoid histology versus gastric adenocarcinoma.
back: * Carcinoid: Organoid, nesting, or trabecular patterns. * Adenocarcinoma: Glandular formation with high pleomorphism and mitoses.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Locate the primary gastric region where Type 1 and Type 2 carcinoids are most frequently found due to cell density.
back: * Fundus and Body. * These regions contain the highest concentration of ECL (histamine-releasing) cells.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
coreConcept: ECL Cell Origin of Gastric Carcinoids
front: The primary cell of origin for gastric carcinoid tumors, characterized by the production of histamine and belonging to the DNES, is the [___] cell.
back: * Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cell. * Part of the Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation (APUD) system. * Proliferates in response to chronic hypergastrinemia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with Pernicious Anemia presents with multiple small yellow polyps in the gastric fundus. Histology shows nests of uniform cells with 'salt-and-pepper' chromatin. What is the underlying pathophysiology?
back: * Type 1 Gastric Carcinoid. * Driven by hypergastrinemia due to achlorhydria. * Results in ECL cell hyperplasia and eventual neoplastic transformation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism that allows cells of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES) to be identified using silver-based histological stains.
back: * Presence of neurosecretory granules with argentaffin or argyrophil properties. * Cells take up amine precursors and decarboxylate them into biogenic amines. * Stains detect the high concentration of matrix proteins.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast Type 1 gastric carcinoid tumors with Type 3 (sporadic) tumors regarding their background gastric pathology and metastatic risk.
back: * Type 1: Background of chronic atrophic gastritis; low metastatic risk; often multiple. * Type 3: Normal background mucosa; high metastatic risk (aggressive); solitary.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Identify the diagnostic immunohistochemical marker that specifically targets the proteins within the matrix of the neurosecretory granules to confirm a carcinoid diagnosis.
back: * Chromogranin A. * Universal marker for neuroendocrine differentiation. * Synaptophysin is a secondary marker targeting synaptic vesicles.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
coreConcept: ECL cell origin of gastric carcinoids
front: The primary histological basis for gastric carcinoid tumors is the neoplastic proliferation of [___] cells within the gastric mucosa.
back: Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells. • These are part of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES). • They are primarily found in the gastric body and fundus.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A 65-year-old male with chronic atrophic gastritis and pernicious anemia is found to have multiple small, yellow-colored subepithelial nodules in the stomach. These are likely [___].
back: Type I Gastric Carcinoids. • These are the most common type (70-80%). • They are associated with hypergastrinemia due to achlorhydria.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain the role of serum gastrin in the development of Type I gastric carcinoid tumors.
back: Gastrin acts as a trophic factor for ECL cells. • Chronic hypergastrinemia causes ECL cell hyperplasia. • Over time, this stimulation leads to dysplasia and carcinoid formation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast the typical clinical presentation and metastatic risk of Type I gastric carcinoids with Type III sporadic gastric carcinoids.
back: Type I: Multiple, small, low metastatic risk (<5%), hypergastrinemia-related. • Type III: Usually solitary, larger, high metastatic risk (>50%), sporadic and aggressive.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Identify the two most reliable immunohistochemical markers used to confirm the neuroendocrine nature of a gastric tumor.
back: Chromogranin A and Synaptophysin. • Chromogranin A is stored in secretory granules. • Synaptophysin is a membrane protein of synaptic-like vesicles.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Histological examination of a gastric carcinoid reveals small, uniform cells with round nuclei and characteristic [___] chromatin.
back: Salt-and-pepper. • This refers to finely clumped, granular chromatin. • It is the classic hallmark of neuroendocrine differentiation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with a solitary 3cm gastric body mass and normal serum gastrin levels undergoes resection. Histology shows nested neuroendocrine cells. This represents a [___].
back: Type III Gastric Carcinoid. • Unlike Type I/II, it is sporadic and gastrin-independent. • It is often more invasive and requires aggressive surgical management.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Describe the electron microscopic hallmark found in the cytoplasm of gastric carcinoid tumor cells.
back: Membrane-bound, dense-core granules. • These granules store amines and peptide hormones. • Their presence confirms the APUD (Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation) nature.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Distinguish the microscopic growth patterns of a gastric carcinoid from a typical gastric adenocarcinoma.
back: Carcinoid: Organoid patterns (nests, ribbons, or cords) of uniform cells. • Adenocarcinoma: Irregular glandular structures with marked pleomorphism and mucin production.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Identify the specific syndrome associated with Type II gastric carcinoids and the underlying clinical cause.
back: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome (ZES). • Often occurs in MEN-1. • Caused by gastrinoma-induced hypergastrinemia stimulating ECL cell growth.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The principal enteroendocrine cells located primarily in the gastric antrum that secrete gastrin to stimulate parietal cell HCl production are called [___].
back:
G Cells.
- Located in Pyloric Antrum.
- Stimulated by peptides, amino acids, and distension.
- Actions: Increases HCl secretion and gastric motility.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A 45-year-old female experiences sharp right upper quadrant pain after consuming a high-fat meal. The hormone responsible for the gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme release seen here is secreted by [___].
back:
I Cells.
- Location: Duodenum and Jejunum.
- Hormone: Cholecystokinin (CCK).
- Action: Gallbladder contraction, pancreatic enzyme secretion, and inhibits gastric emptying.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Describe the mechanism by which S cells in the duodenum respond to a decrease in luminal pH below 4.5.
back:
- Secretes Secretin.
- Stimulates pancreatic ductal cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid.
- Inhibits gastric acid (HCl) secretion.
- Neutralizes acidic chyme for enzyme activity.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the primary incretin hormones produced by K cells versus L cells regarding their location and action.
back:
- K Cells: Produce GIP; located in Duodenum/Jejunum.
- L Cells: Produce GLP-1; located in Ileum/Colon.
- Both stimulate insulin release in response to glucose.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Identify the universal inhibitory enteroendocrine cell and its primary paracrine action within the GI mucosa.
back:
D Cells.
- Hormone: Somatostatin.
- Action: Inhibits release of all GI hormones (Gastrin, CCK, Secretin) and HCl secretion.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The enteroendocrine cells that produce serotonin to regulate gut motility and are the origin of classic carcinoid tumors are [___].
back:
EC (Enterochromaffin) Cells.
- Also called Kulchitsky cells.
- Location: Stomach, Small and Large Intestine.
- Action: Increases gut peristalsis.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient presents with persistent watery diarrhea and hypokalemia. Lab findings suggest a VIPoma. Identify the cell type and hormone action involved in this clinical scenario.
back:
D1 Cells.
- Hormone: Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP).
- Action: Stimulates intestinal water/electrolyte secretion and smooth muscle relaxation.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the physiological significance of Motilin secretion by Mo cells during the interdigestive state.
back:
- Produced in Duodenum/Jejunum.
- Initiates Migrating Motor Complex (MMC).
- Action: Clears undigested debris ('housekeeping' function) between meals.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast 'Open type' and 'Closed type' enteroendocrine cells based on their microscopic relationship with the lumen.
back:
- Open Type: Reach the lumen via apical microvilli; act as chemoreceptors.
- Closed Type: No luminal contact; stimulated by basal distension or nerves.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Specify the common biochemical characteristic of DNES cells represented by the acronym 'APUD'.
back:
Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation.
- Cells take up precursors (e.g. Tryptophan).
- Decarboxylate them into biogenic amines (e.g. Serotonin).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The enteroendocrine cells that exhibit a high affinity for chromium salts and are the primary source of serotonin in the GI tract are [___].
back:
• Enterochromaffin (EC) cells (or Kulchitsky cells).
• Part of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES).
• Action: Increases gut motility.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient presents with recurrent peptic ulcers and extremely high serum gastrin levels (Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome). The enteroendocrine cells primarily responsible for this hormone are located in the [___].
back:
• G cells.
• Primarily located in the gastric antrum and duodenum.
• Action: Stimulates HCl secretion from parietal cells.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
coreConcept: S Cell Function and pH Regulation
front: Explain the role of duodenal S cells in maintaining the pH balance of the small intestine.
back:
• Secrete Secretin in response to acidic chyme (low pH).
• Stimulates pancreatic duct cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid.
• Neutralizes stomach acid in the duodenum.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A 50-year-old patient experiences abdominal cramping that correlates with the Migrating Motor Complex (MMC) during fasting. Contrast the hormone responsible for this with the one that inhibits gastric emptying.
back:
• Motilin (M cells): Initiates MMCs and intestinal motility.
• GIP (K cells): Inhibits gastric motility and acid secretion while stimulating insulin.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Identify the 'Incretin' hormone produced by L cells in the ileum and its primary physiological action.
back:
• Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1).
• Stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion.
• Delays gastric emptying and induces satiety.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The biochemical classification [___] describes cells with the capability to take up amine precursors and decarboxylate them into biogenic amines.
back:
• APUD cells (Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation).
• Characterizes most enteroendocrine/DNES cells.
• Example: Tryptophan to Serotonin conversion.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient consumes a high-fat meal. Which specific enteroendocrine cell type is stimulated, and what are its two major actions on the biliary and pancreatic systems?
back:
• I cells (Duodenum/Jejunum).
• Hormone: Cholecystokinin (CCK).
• Actions: Gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Describe the local 'paracrine' mechanism by which D cells regulate gastric acid secretion.
back:
• D cells secrete Somatostatin.
• Acts locally to inhibit Gastrin release (from G cells) and HCl release (from Parietal cells).
• Functions as the universal GI 'off-switch'.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the stimuli that trigger Secretin release (S cells) vs Cholecystokinin release (I cells).
back:
• S cells: Triggered primarily by low pH (acidic chyme).
• I cells: Triggered primarily by fatty acids and amino acids in the duodenum.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Name the hormone produced by K cells and its unique role in the 'entero-insular axis'.
back:
• Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Peptide (GIP).
• Role: Enhances insulin release from pancreatic Beta cells in response to oral glucose load.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The principal enteroendocrine cells located in the gastric antrum that secrete gastrin to stimulate hydrochloric acid production are known as [___].
back: G cells. *Location: Gastric antrum and pylorus. *Hormone: Gastrin. *Actions: Stimulates parietal cells to secrete HCl and increases gastric motility.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient presents with impaired fat digestion and gallbladder stasis. Biopsy reveals a deficiency in enteroendocrine cells within the duodenum. Which hormone do these cells normally produce?
back: Cholecystokinin (CCK). *Cell Type: I cells. *Action: Stimulates gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion. *Trigger: Presence of fatty acids and amino acids in the duodenum.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the role of S cells in maintaining duodenal pH when acidic chyme enters from the stomach.
back: Secretin Release: *Trigger: Low pH (acidic chyme) in the duodenum. *Action: Stimulates pancreatic duct cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid. *Effect: Neutralizes gastric acid to protect duodenal mucosa.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the primary stimuli and metabolic actions of K cells versus L cells found in the intestinal mucosa.
back: K cells: Found in proximal small intestine; secrete GIP to stimulate insulin release. *L cells: Found in distal ileum/colon; secrete GLP-1 to enhance insulin secretion and induce satiety.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Name the specific biogenic amine produced by Enterochromaffin (EC) cells and its primary effect on gastrointestinal physiology.
back: Serotonin (5-HT). *Type: Amine-producing APUD cell. *Action: Primary regulator of the peristaltic reflex and gut motility. *Feature: Shows affinity for silver (Argentaffin) or chromium salts.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Enteroendocrine cells categorized as [___] cells are primarily located in the stomach pylorus and secrete Gastrin to stimulate parietal cell HCL production.
back:
• G cells
• Location: Stomach (Pyloric antrum), Duodenum
• Action: Stimulates gastric acid secretion and mucosal growth.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A 45-year-old male presents with recurrent peptic ulcers and diarrhea. Labs show hypergastrinemia. This condition involves the neoplastic proliferation of [___] cells.
back:
• G cells (Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome)
• Location: Duodenum or Pancreas (ectopic)
• Action: Excessive Gastrin leads to massive acid hypersecretion.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the physiological mechanism of S-cells in the duodenum when intraluminal pH drops below 4.5.
back:
• Hormone: Secretin
• Action: Stimulates pancreatic and biliary bicarbonate secretion
• Result: Neutralizes acidic chyme and inhibits Gastrin release.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast I-cells and S-cells based on their primary hormonal triggers and downstream effects on the pancreas.
back:
• I-cells: Triggered by fatty acids/peptides; release CCK (enzyme secretion).
• S-cells: Triggered by low pH; release Secretin (HCO3- secretion).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Name the paracrine enteroendocrine cell that acts as a 'universal inhibitor' by secreting Somatostatin in response to low pH.
back:
• D cells
• Location: Stomach, Small Intestine, Pancreas
• Action: Inhibits release of Gastrin, Secretin, CCK, and Insulin.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Enteroendocrine cells found in the proximal small intestine that secrete Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) to induce the 'incretin effect' are [___] cells.
back:
• K cells
• Location: Duodenum and Jejunum
• Action: Stimulates glucose-dependent insulin release; inhibits gastric HCL.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient presents with episodic skin flushing, wheezing, and right-sided heart murmurs. A midgut tumor is suspected. This clinical triad results from overactivity of [___].
back:
• Enterochromaffin (EC) cells / Kulchitsky cells
• Hormone: Serotonin (5-HT)
• Action: Increases GI motility and stimulates intestinal secretion.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain how Mo-cells regulate the Migrating Motor Complex (MMC) during the fasting state.
back:
• Hormone: Motilin
• Location: Duodenum and Jejunum
• Action: Initiates peristaltic waves to clear the GI tract of debris.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Distinguish between 'Open' and 'Closed' type enteroendocrine cells based on their microscopic morphology and interaction with chyme.
back:
• Open: Reach the lumen with microvilli (chemosensors).
• Closed: Do not reach the lumen; base of glands (paracrine/neural triggers).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Identify the distal small intestine cells that produce GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide 1) to enhance satiety and slow gastric emptying.
back:
• L cells
• Location: Ileum and Colon
• Action: Stimulates insulin release; inhibits glucagon; promotes satiety.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The primary biogenic amine produced by [___] cells in the intestinal mucosa through the decarboxylation of tryptophan is serotonin.
back:
• Enterochromaffin (EC) cells
• Also known as Kulchitsky cells
• Identified by affinity for chromium salts.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A 10-year-old child presents with polyuria, polyphagia, and hyperglycemia. Histological analysis of the pancreas would likely reveal an absence of [___].
back:
• Beta (B) cells
• Normally occupy 70% of the islet
• Located in the central region of Islets of Langerhans.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Alpha cells respond to hypoglycemia.
back:
• Secrete Glucagon
• Stimulates hepatic glycogenolysis
• Increases gluconeogenesis to raise blood glucose.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the typical histological location of Alpha cells and Beta cells within a human Islet of Langerhans.
back:
• Alpha (A) cells: Periphery of the islet (20%)
• Beta (B) cells: Central region (70%)
• Both associated with fenestrated capillaries.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Identify the biochemical processes represented by the acronym APUD in the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System.
back:
• Amine Precursor Uptake
• Decarboxylation
• Converts amino acids (e.g., tryptophan) into biogenic amines.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The paracrine hormone [___] is secreted by Delta (D) cells and serves to inhibit both insulin and glucagon release.
back:
• Somatostatin
• Found scattered in pancreatic islets
• Constitutes 5-10% of total islet cells.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient with a tumor in the head of the pancreas presents with impaired inhibition of exocrine pancreatic secretion. This involves the [___] cells.
back:
• PP cells (Pancreatic Polypeptide cells)
• Located primarily in the pancreatic head
• Constitute 1-2% of total cells.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Describe the intracellular mechanism used by Enteroendocrine cells to produce biogenic amines like serotonin.
back:
• Take up amino acid precursors (tryptophan)
• Undergo enzymatic decarboxylation
• Store products in membrane-bound secretory granules.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the delivery mechanism of Endocrine communication versus Paracrine communication.
back:
• Endocrine: Hormones enter blood/lymph for remote targets
• Paracrine: Hormones diffuse through extracellular fluid to neighboring targets.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Specify the staining characteristic that allows Enterochromaffin cells to be visualized in histological sections.
back:
• Affinity for chromium salts
• Develops a brown color with potassium dichromate
• Part of the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES).

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Embryologically, the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) originates as an outpocketing of oral ectoderm known as [___].
back:
• Rathke's pouch
• Grows cranially from the stomodeum
• Eventually detaches to form pars distalis, intermedia, and tuberalis.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A 40-year-old male presents with enlarging hands, feet, and a prominent lower jaw. A pituitary adenoma is suspected. Which cell type is likely hyperactive?
back:
• Somatotrophs
• Located in pars distalis
• Acidophilic cells that secrete Growth Hormone (GH)
• Condition: Acromegaly.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Explain the biological function of Herring bodies found in the neurohypophysis.
back:
• Store neurosecretory granules
• Contain ADH (vasopressin) and Oxytocin
• Appear as irregular basophilic masses near fenestrated capillaries
• Represent dilated axonal terminals.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Contrast the hormones secreted by Acidophils versus Basophils in the pars distalis.
back:
• Acidophils: GH (Somatotrophs) and Prolactin (Lactotrophs)
• Basophils: ACTH (Corticotrophs), TSH (Thyrotrophs), and FSH/LH (Gonadotrophs).

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Identify the specialized glial cells that provide structural support to the unmyelinated axons in the pars nervosa.
back:
• Pituicytes
• Resemble astrocytes
• Possess long cytoplasmic processes
• Ensheath axonal terminals near blood vessels.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Chromophils that have released their secretory granules and are in a temporary resting phase appear as [___] under light microscopy.
back:
• Chromophobes
• Stain poorly
• Cytoplasm lacks secretory granules
• Constitute a major cell population in pars distalis.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A postpartum female is unable to produce milk despite frequent suckling. A defect in which hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal mechanism is likely involved?
back:
• Oxytocin release
• Synthesized in paraventricular/supraoptic nuclei
• Transported via hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract
• Released from pars nervosa to trigger milk ejection.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: How do the cells of the pars intermedia (Melanotrophs) synthesize multiple hormones from a single precursor?
back:
• Proteolytic cleavage of Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)
• Generates MSH, ACTH, and endorphins
• Basophilic polygonal cells arranged in cords.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Distinguish between the primary mode of hormone delivery to the Adenohypophysis versus the Neurohypophysis.
back:
• Adenohypophysis: Hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal system (vascular)
• Neurohypophysis: Hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract (axonal/neural transport).

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Where are the hormones released by the posterior pituitary (ADH and Oxytocin) actually synthesized?
back:
• Hypothalamus
• Supraoptic and Paraventricular nuclei
• Pars nervosa acts only as a storage depot (not a gland).

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: The histological basis of gastric carcinoid tumors involves cells of the [___] system, which are identified by their affinity for chromium salts.
back: • Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES). • Also known as Enterochromaffin (EC) or Kulchitsky cells. • Derived from the embryological neural crest.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A 65-year-old with long-standing Pernicious Anemia presents with multiple 4mm yellow submucosal fundic polyps showing 'salt and pepper' chromatin. The likely pathology is [___].
back: • Type 1 Gastric Carcinoid. • Associated with chronic atrophic gastritis. • Driven by chronic hypergastrinemia.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Contrast the stimulus for hyperplasia in Type 1 Gastric Carcinoids versus Sporadic (Type 3) tumors.
back: • Type 1: Stimulated by chronic hypergastrinemia (loss of acid feedback). • Type 3: Sporadic mutation, not gastrin-dependent. • Type 1 is usually multifactorial and benign, Type 3 is solitary and aggressive.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: A patient with a large solitary gastric mass and liver metastases presents with episodic flushing and diarrhea. Distinguish this from typical gastric carcinoids based on systemic manifestation.
back: • Diagnosis: Carcinoid Syndrome. • Occurs when serotonin bypasses first-pass metabolism via liver metastasis. • Histology shows 'Salt and Pepper' chromatin and organoid nests.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Name the primary biogenic amine secreted by gastric EC cells and the IHC marker used to detect its associated dense-core granules.
back: • Hormone: Serotonin (5-HT). • Marker: Chromogranin A or Synaptophysin. • Reflects secretory activity of DNES cells.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: The characteristic nuclear appearance of uniform neuroendocrine cells in a carcinoid tumor is described as [___].
back: • Salt and Pepper Chromatin. • Represents finely clumped chromatin with clear interspaces. • Distinct from the pleomorphism seen in adenocarcinomas.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: In a patient with Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome (MEN1), identify the mechanism leading to the secondary development of multiple small gastric carcinoids.
back: • Gastrin-producing tumor (gastrinoma) stimulates ECL cells. • Results in chronic ECL cell hyperplasia. • Progressive neoplastic transformation into Type 2 Carcinoids.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Explain how the lack of parietal cell-mediated acid secretion in atrophic gastritis leads to ECL cell transformation.
back: • Loss of acid results in loss of negative feedback to G-cells. • Persistent high Gastrin causes trophic stimulation of ECL cells. • Leads to a hyperplasia-dysplasia-carcinoma sequence.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Detail the metabolic loop involving Gastrin and Enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells in the pathogenesis of Type 1 Carcinoids.
back: • Achlorhydria stimulates G-cells in the antrum. • Elevated Gastrin binds CCK-2 receptors on fundic ECL cells. • Chronic trophic signaling triggers neoplastic growth.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Gastric Carcinoid Tumors
front: Name the specialized cytoplasmic structures visualized on electron microscopy that are diagnostic of the neuroendocrine origin of carcinoids.
back: • Dense-core neurosecretory granules. • Measure 100-300 nm in diameter. • Contain hormones and biogenic amines.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The specific group of enteroendocrine cells characterized by their ability to take up amine precursors and convert them into biogenic amines are termed [___] cells.
back:
• APUD cells (Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation).
• Key example: Decarboxylation of tryptophan to serotonin.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A biopsy of the gastric mucosa reveals scattered cells that exhibit a distinct brown color when stained with potassium dichromate. Identify these cells and the specific chemical affinity responsible.
back:
• Enterochromaffin (EC) cells or Kulchitsky cells.
• Affinity for chromium salts (chromaffin reaction).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the role of the 'Amine Precursor Uptake and Decarboxylation' mechanism in the production of serotonin by DNES cells.
back:
• Tryptophan is taken up by the cell as an amine precursor.
• It undergoes decarboxylation to form serotonin (a biogenic amine/neurotransmitter).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the mode of 'paracrine' communication with 'juxtacrine' communication as utilized by enteroendocrine cells.
back:
• Paracrine: Hormones diffuse through extracellular fluid to reach neighboring target cells.
• Juxtacrine: Messengers interact directly with receptors on the surface of an adjacent cell.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Identify the primary anatomical locations where enteroendocrine cells are found scattered among exocrine secretory cells.
back:
• Mucosa of the stomach.
• Mucosa of the small and large intestines.
• Mucosa of the bronchi (respiratory tract).

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: The biogenic amine [___], derived from the amino acid tryptophan, is a major signaling molecule produced by enterochromaffin cells.
back:
• Serotonin.
• Functions as a neurotransmitter and local hormone in the digestive tract.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: A patient presents with a tumor of the 'Diffuse Neuroendocrine System' (DNES). Based on cell morphology, where are these secretory cells typically found in relation to other epithelial cells?
back:
• Scattered individually among exocrine secretory cells.
• Part of the mucosa, rather than forming discrete glands.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Explain the physiological significance of the 'autocrine' mode of action in neuroendocrine signaling.
back:
• Chemical messengers produced by the cell bind to receptors on its own surface.
• Allows for self-regulation of secretory activity.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Contrast the transport mechanism and receptor location of steroid hormones versus protein hormones produced by endocrine cells.
back:
• Steroid: Lipid-soluble, diffuses through membranes, binds intracellular receptors (nucleus/cytoplasm).
• Protein: Water-soluble, cannot cross membranes, binds cell surface receptors.

category: Classify the principal Enteroendocrine Cells on the basis of type, location, hormone produced and Actions
front: Name the four chemical classes of hormones used by the endocrine system for cellular integration.
back:
• Steroid hormones.
• Protein/Peptide hormones.
• Amino acid-derivatives.
• Arachidonic acid-derivatives (Prostaglandins/Leukotrienes).

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: The adenohypophysis develops from an outpocketing of the oral ectoderm known as [___].
back: Rathke's pouch. It grows cranially from the primitive oral cavity (stomodeum) to meet the neurohypophysis.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A 10-year-old child presents with gigantism due to a pituitary tumor. Histological examination would most likely reveal an over-proliferation of which specific cell subtype in the pars distalis?
back:
Somatotrophs. 
- These are acidophils (~50% of cells).
- They secrete growth hormone (somatotropin).
- Granules measure 300-400 nm.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Explain the role of the pituicyte in the microscopic organization of the neurohypophysis.
back:
Pituicytes are specialized glial cells (similar to astrocytes) that:
- Provide structural support to unmyelinated axons.
- Ensheath axonal terminals.
- End in close relation to fenestrated capillaries.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A patient with symptoms of hyperprolactinemia undergoes biopsy. Contrast the staining and morphology of the affected cells with those that secrete TSH.
back:
Lactotrophs (affected): Acidophilic staining; large 600nm granules; polygonal shape.
Thyrotrophs (TSH): Basophilic staining; small 150nm granules; large oval shape.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Identify the neurohypophyseal hormone that acts on the collecting ducts of the kidney and is stored in Herring bodies.
back:
Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH/Vasopressin).
- Synthesized in supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
- Transported via the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract.
- Stored in Herring bodies.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Cells in the pars distalis that appear pale and lack secretory granules because they are in a temporary resting phase are called [___].
back: Chromophobes. These cells have already released their granules and show little affinity for acidic or basic dyes.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: An adult presents with enlarged facial features and hands (acromegaly). Histologically, the tumor arises from cells that stain [___] with acidic dyes.
back: Acidophilic. Specifically, Somatotrophs in the pars distalis which secrete excess Growth Hormone (GH) after the closure of epiphyseal plates.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Explain the significance of Herring bodies as seen under the light microscope.
back:
They are basophilic masses of irregular shape representing:
- Exceptionally large axonal swellings.
- Sites of hormone accumulation (ADH/Oxytocin).
- Located close to fenestrated capillaries in the pars nervosa.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Contrast the primary secretory product of the Pars Intermedia with that of the Gonadotrophs in the Pars Distalis.
back:
Pars Intermedia: Melanotrophs produce POMC (cleaved into MSH, ACTH, endorphins).
Gonadotrophs: Produce FSH and LH (Glycoprotein hormones regulating gonadal function).

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Identify the two nuclei of the hypothalamus that synthesize hormones for the neurohypophysis.
back: Supraoptic and Paraventricular nuclei. Their axons form the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract passing through the infundibulum.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: The embryonic outpocketing of oral ectoderm that gives rise to the adenohypophysis is known as [___].
back:
* Rathke's pouch
* Originates from the primitive oral cavity (stomodeum)
* Residual lumen forms the narrow pituitary fissure
* Thickened anterior wall becomes the pars distalis

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: An adult patient presents with progressively enlarging hands, feet, and a prominent lower jaw. This clinical condition results from an adenoma of which specific cells in the pars distalis?
back:
* Somatotrophs
* Causes overproduction of Growth Hormone (GH)
* Termed Acromegaly in adults
* Cells appear acidophilic in standard histological sections

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Explain the storage and transport mechanism for hormones released by the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis).
back:
* Synthesized in hypothalamic nuclei (supraoptic and paraventricular)
* Transported via the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract
* Stored in axonal terminals (Herring bodies)
* Released into fenestrated blood capillaries

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Contrast the histological appearance and functional significance of Chromophobes versus Chromophils in the pars distalis.
back:
* Chromophils: Stain well (Acidophils/Basophils); contain abundant secretory granules
* Chromophobes: Stain poorly; lack secretory granules
* Functional state: Chromophobes are typically degranulated chromophils in a resting phase

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Identify the primary cell type found in the pars intermedia and the specific protein precursor they synthesize.
back:
* Melanotrophs
* Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)
* Cleaved into ACTH, endorphins, and MSH
* Organized as cords of basophilic polygonal cells

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: The specialized glial cells found within the pars nervosa that provide structural support to unmyelinated axons are termed [___].
back:
* Pituicytes
* Resemble astrocytes histologically
* Contain abundant glial intermediate filaments
* Processes end near axons or fenestrated capillaries

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A histological slide shows basophilic, irregular masses close to blood capillaries in the pars nervosa. Identify these structures and their contents.
back:
* Herring bodies
* Dilated axonal terminals
* Contain membrane-bound neurosecretory granules
* Store Oxytocin or Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Differentiate the roles of Gonadotrophs in males versus females regarding their target cells in the gonads.
back:
* FSH: Stimulates ovarian follicles (Females); supports Sertoli cells (Males)
* LH: Stimulates ovulation/corpus luteum (Females); stimulates Leydig cells (Males)
* Cells are classified as basophils

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Distinguish between Acidophils and Basophils in the pars distalis by listing the five functional cell varieties assigned to each group.
back:
* Acidophils: Somatotrophs (GH) and Lactotrophs (Prolactin)
* Basophils: Corticotrophs (ACTH), Gonadotrophs (FSH/LH), and Thyrotrophs (TSH)
* Acidophils generally stain red/orange; Basophils stain bluish

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Specify the anatomical components of the neurohypophysis and their specific embryonic origin.
back:
* Components: Infundibulum and Pars nervosa
* Origin: Neuroectoderm
* Arises as a ventral evagination from the floor of the diencephalon

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: The cells of the pars distalis that exhibit a strong affinity for acidic dyes and are responsible for secreting Growth Hormone and Prolactin are [___].
back:
Acidophils
* Includes Somatotrophs (GH)
* Includes Lactotrophs/Mammotrophs (Prolactin)
* Constitute roughly 65-70% of chromophils.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: An adult male presents with enlarged hands, feet, and a prominent lower jaw. Hypersecretion of which specific pituitary cell type is the most likely cause of this pathology?
back:
Somatotrophs
* Secrete Growth Hormone (Somatotropin)
* Causes Acromegaly in adults
* Causes Gigantism in children.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Explain the mechanism by which Vasopressin and Oxytocin reach the systemic circulation from the neurohypophysis.
back:
Synthesized in hypothalamus (Supraoptic/Paraventricular nuclei)
* Transported via Hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract
* Stored in Herring bodies (axonal swellings)
* Released into fenestrated capillaries of Pars Nervosa.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Contrast the functional status and staining characteristics of Chromophils versus Chromophobes in the pars distalis.
back:
Chromophils:
* Stain well due to active secretory granules
* Subdivided into Acidophils and Basophils
Chromophobes:
* Stain poorly; lack granules
* Represent depleted or resting-phase chromophils.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Identify the hormone secreted by the least abundant cell type in the pars distalis and its primary target gland.
back:
Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH)
* Produced by Thyrotrophs (~5% of cells)
* Targets follicular cells of the Thyroid gland
* Stimulates T3/T4 synthesis and release.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: The narrow zone of the adenohypophysis containing follicles and cords of melanotrophs that synthesize Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) is the [___].
back:
Pars Intermedia
* Found between pars distalis and neurohypophysis
* Produces MSH, ACTH, and endorphins via POMC cleavage.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: A 30-year-old female presents with galactorrhea (inappropriate milk production) and amenorrhea. This clinical presentation suggests hypersecretion from which pituitary cell variety?
back:
Lactotrophs (Mammotrophs)
* Acidophilic cells
* Secrete Prolactin
* Stimulate mammary development and lactation; inhibits GnRH.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: How do the hormones produced by Gonadotrophs differ in their physiological roles in males versus females?
back:
FSH:
* Females: Ovarian follicle growth
* Males: Sertoli cell support
LH:
* Females: Ovulation/Corpus luteum formation
* Males: Leydig cell/Testosterone stimulation.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Distinguish the embryological origins of the Adenohypophysis and the Neurohypophysis.
back:
Adenohypophysis:
* Derived from oral ectoderm (Rathke’s pouch)
Neurohypophysis:
* Derived from neuroectoderm (ventral evagination of diencephalon).

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Identify the specialized glial cells of the neurohypophysis and their primary function.
back:
Pituicytes
* Resemble astrocytes
* Provide physical and metabolic support to unmyelinated axons
* Processes end in close relation to blood vessels.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: The most abundant cell type in the pars distalis, comprising approximately 50% of the total population and staining acidophilic, is the [___].
back:
• **Somatotroph**
• Secretes Growth Hormone (GH/Somatotropin).
• Functions to stimulate general body growth and metabolic processes.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: A 10-year-old boy presents with an abnormally tall stature and a benign tumor in the sella turcica. The specific pituitary cell type over-secreting hormone in this patient is the [___].
back:
• **Somatotroph**
• Condition: Gigantism (Pituitary Adenoma).
• Mechanism: Excess GH stimulates epiphyseal plates before closure.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Explain the biological source and transport mechanism of hormones released from the neurohypophysis.
back:
• **Hypothalamic Source**: Synthesized in Supraoptic/Paraventricular nuclei.
• **Transport**: Carried via unmyelinated axons (Hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract).
• **Storage**: Released into capillaries from Herring bodies (dilated terminals).

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Contrast the hormone profiles of Acidophils versus Basophils in the pars distalis.
back:
• **Acidophils**: Produce GH (Somatotrophs) and Prolactin (Lactotrophs).
• **Basophils**: Produce ACTH (Corticotrophs), TSH (Thyrotrophs), and FSH/LH (Gonadotrophs).

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Identify the specific basophilic cell type responsible for regulating thyroid activity and its primary hormone.
back:
• **Thyrotroph**
• Hormone: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH/Thyrotropin).
• Function: Stimulates thyroid follicles to synthesize T3 and T4.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: The embryological outpocketing of oral ectoderm that gives rise to the entire adenohypophysis is known as [___].
back:
• **Rathke's Pouch**
• Forms: Pars distalis, pars intermedia, and pars tuberalis.
• Contrast: Neurohypophysis arises from neuroectoderm (diencephalon floor).

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: A 28-year-old female presents with galactorrhea and infertility. Hyperplasia of which pituitary cell type is most likely responsible?
back:
• **Lactotroph (Mammotroph)**
• Hormone: Prolactin.
• Function: Promotes mammary development and milk production.
• Prolactinoma leads to reproductive dysfunction via GnRH inhibition.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: How do Melanotrophs of the pars intermedia contribute to hormonal regulation via Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)?
back:
• **POMC Cleavage**: Melanotrophs synthesize POMC protein.
• **Products**: Proteolytic cleavage generates MSH (Melanocyte-Stimulating Hormone).
• **Other**: Also produces ACTH and endorphins.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Distinguish between Chromophobes and Chromophils based on their histological appearance and functional state.
back:
• **Chromophils**: Stain well; contain secretory granules (active/storing).
• **Chromophobes**: Stain poorly; lack granules; represent resting/depleted cells.

category: Classify pituitary gland on the basis of cell type, hormone produced and functions
front: Describe the anatomical features and role of Pituicytes within the neurohypophysis.
back:
• **Pituicytes**: Specialized glial cells (modified astrocytes).
• **Feature**: Possess long processes ending on blood vessels.
• **Role**: Provide physical and metabolic support to hypothalamic axons.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: The adenohypophysis originates from the [___], an outpocketing of oral ectoderm from the primitive stomodeum.
back:
* Rathke's pouch
* Grows cranially to meet the neurohypophysis
* Eventually detaches from the stomodeum

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: An adult male presents with an enlarged lower jaw, hands, and feet. Histological examination of the pituitary would likely reveal a benign tumor of [___].
back:
* Somatotrophs (Acidophils)
* Secrete Growth Hormone
* Condition: Acromegaly

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: How do chromophobes differ from chromophils in terms of their secretory status and appearance in the pars distalis?
back:
* Chromophobes: Stain poorly; lack granules; represent resting or degranulated chromophils.
* Chromophils: Stain well (Acidophils/Basophils); contain hormone-filled secretory granules.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A biopsy shows a pituitary tumor staining intensely with acidic dyes. Contrast the two specific cell types that could be responsible for this finding.
back:
* Somatotrophs: Secrete Somatotropin (GH); 300-400nm granules.
* Lactotrophs (Mammotrophs): Secrete Prolactin; larger 600nm granules.
* Both are Acidophils.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Identify the site of synthesis for the hormones stored in the pars nervosa and the specific bundle used for their delivery.
back:
* Synthesis: Supraoptic and Paraventricular nuclei (Hypothalamus).
* Delivery: Hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract (unmyelinated axons).
* Stored as Herring bodies.

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: The specialized glial cells in the pars nervosa that provide structural support and contain glial intermediate filaments are called [___].
back:
* Pituicytes
* Resemble astrocytes
* Support 100,000+ unmyelinated axons

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: A 12-year-old child exhibits gigantism due to a tumor. Overactivity is most likely occurring in cells that normally constitute [___]% of the pars distalis.
back:
* 50% (Somatotrophs)
* Most abundant cell type
* Secrete Growth Hormone

category: Describe microscopic structure of Pituitary gland
front: Describe the formation and content of Herring bodies, explaining why the neurohypophysis is not a 'true' endocrine gland.
back:
* Formation: Dilated axonal terminals of hypothalamic neurons.
* Content: Oxytocin and ADH (Vasopressin).
* Distinction: It only stores hormones; synthesis occurs in the hypothalamus.
