● Transition Zone: Site of BPH; causes early urethral obstruction/urinary symptoms
● Peripheral Zone: Site of most cancers; often asymptomatic early as it is distant from the urethra

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the acidophilic, lamellated bodies found within prostatic acini that increase in number with advancing age.
back:
● Corpora amylacea (Prostatic concretions)
● Represent condensed glycoproteins and cell fragments
● May partially calcify in older individuals

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The [___] zone of the prostate contains submucosal glands whose ducts must pass through the transition zone to reach the prostatic urethra.
back:
● Central Zone
● Constitutes ~25% of the prostatic volume
● Located between the transition and peripheral zones

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A patient presents with an elevated serum Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA). Identify the specific enzyme and its normal histological function.
back:
● Serine Protease
● Function: Liquefies coagulated semen after deposition in the vagina
● Normally leaks in small amounts from stroma into blood

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the histological changes that occur in the transition zone after the age of 40 that lead to 'nodular hyperplasia'.
back:
● Hyperplasia of both glandular acini and fibromuscular stroma
● Results in formation of nodules of varying sizes
● Leads to partial or complete urethral obstruction

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the ductal anatomy of the 'mucosal glands' versus the 'main glands' of the prostate.
back:
● Mucosal Glands: Short ducts opening directly into the urethra (Transition Zone)
● Main Glands: Long ducts passing through multiple zones (Peripheral Zone)

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Name the non-glandular component of the prostate that occupies the anterior region where the peripheral zone is deficient.
back:
● Anterior fibromuscular stroma
● Composed of thick collagenous tissue and smooth muscle fibers
● Lacks glandular acini

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) predominantly involves the [___] zone of the prostate gland.
back:
Transition Zone
* Contains mucosal glands.
* Surrounds the proximal urethra.
* Hyperplasia leads to urethral obstruction.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 70-year-old male presents with a hard nodule on digital rectal examination. Biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. This malignancy most commonly originates in the [___] zone.
back:
Peripheral Zone
* Largest zone (~70% volume).
* Contains 'Main Glands' with long ducts.
* Site for 80% of prostatic cancers.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) levels increase in the blood during prostatitis or cancer.
back:
* PSA is a serine protease normally secreted into acini.
* Tissue inflammation or malignancy disrupts the epithelial-stromal barrier.
* This allows the enzyme to leak into the prostatic stroma and enter the bloodstream.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the Transition Zone and the Peripheral Zone in terms of volume and specific glandular type.
back:
* Transition Zone: ~5% volume; contains Mucosal glands.
* Peripheral Zone: ~70% volume; contains Main glands.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the tissue components that constitute the fibromuscular stroma of the prostate.
back:
* Abundant smooth muscle fibers.
* Dense irregular connective tissue.
* Collagen and elastic fibers.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The acidophilic, concentrically lamellated bodies representing condensed glycoproteins in prostatic acini are called [___].
back:
Corpora Amylacea
* Also called prostatic concretions.
* Increase in number with age.
* May become partially calcified.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A patient presents with nocturia and a weak urinary stream. Histology shows nodular hyperplasia. Which zone's specific glands are primarily responsible for these obstructive symptoms?
back:
Transition Zone (Mucosal Glands)
* Their innermost location around the urethra causes compression upon enlargement.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the anatomical relationship of the 'Main Glands' ducts as they pass through the prostate to the urethra.
back:
* Originate in the Peripheral Zone.
* Possess long ducts.
* Must pass through the Central and Transition zones to reach the prostatic urethra.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Distinguish the Central Zone from the Transition Zone based on its volume and glandular classification.
back:
* Central Zone: ~25% volume; contains Submucosal glands.
* Transition Zone: ~5% volume; contains Mucosal glands.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Name the non-glandular region that replaces the peripheral zone in the anterior aspect of the prostate.
back:
Anterior Fibromuscular Stroma
* Thick layer of fibromuscular tissue.
* Completely lacks glandular elements.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) predominantly originates in the [___] zone of the prostate, frequently leading to urethral compression.
back:
Transition Zone
- Contains mucosal glands.
- Surrounds the prostatic urethra.
- Hyperplasia here causes early obstructive symptoms.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 65-year-old male complains of a weak urinary stream and nocturia. On examination, the prostate is enlarged but non-nodular. Identify the specific glandular zone responsible for these obstructive symptoms.
back:
Transition Zone
- Smallest zone in young men (~5%).
- Site of nodular hyperplasia.
- Compresses the prostatic urethra leading to urinary retention.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) becomes a serum marker for prostatic pathologies.
back:
- PSA (serine protease) is normally secreted into acini.
- Small amounts leak into stromal capillaries.
- Architecture disruption (cancer/prostatitis) increases leakage into systemic circulation.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A hard, fixed nodule is palpated on the posterior aspect of the prostate during a digital rectal exam. Contrast the likely anatomical zone and pathology of this finding with BPH.
back:
- Zone: Peripheral Zone (posterior aspect).
- Pathology: Prostatic Adenocarcinoma (Cancer).
- Contrast: BPH occurs in the central Transition Zone and is usually rubbery/smooth.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the non-glandular component that replaces the peripheral zone in the anterior aspect of the prostate.
back:
Anterior Fibromuscular Stroma
- Thick layer of dense connective tissue.
- Contains smooth muscle fibers.
- Lacks glandular acini.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Approximately 80% of prostatic adenocarcinomas originate within the [___] zone of the gland.
back:
Peripheral Zone
- Largest zone (~70% glandular tissue).
- Contains the "main glands".
- Possesses long ducts opening into the urethra.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A patient presents with pelvic pain and a significantly elevated PSA. Biopsy shows inflammation but no malignancy. Relate this presentation to the leakage of prostatic enzymes.
back:
Prostatitis
- Acute or chronic inflammation.
- Causes breakdown of the blood-prostate barrier.
- Results in PSA (serine protease) leaking into the bloodstream.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the physiological role of fibrinolysin and serine protease in the composition of prostatic fluid.
back:
- Secreted into the seminal fluid (20-30% volume).
- Function: Facilitate the liquefaction of coagulated semen.
- Occurs after deposition in the acidic vaginal environment.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Distinguish between the glands found in the transition zone and those found in the peripheral zone based on duct morphology.
back:
- Transition Zone: Mucosal glands; short ducts opening directly into urethra.
- Peripheral Zone: Main glands; long ducts passing through central and transition zones.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the acidophilic, lamellated proteinaceous concretions typically found in the lumina of geriatric prostatic acini.
back:
Corpora Amylacea
- Also called prostatic concretions.
- Composed of glycoproteins and calcium.
- Number increases significantly with age.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The innermost zone of the prostate, surrounding the urethra and representing the primary site for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH), is the [___].
back:
● Transition Zone
● Contains mucosal glands
● Makes up ~5% of prostatic volume in young males

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 65-year-old male presents with urinary frequency, nocturia, and a weak stream. Digital rectal exam reveals a smooth, firm enlargement. Which prostatic zone is pathologically involved?
back:
● Transition Zone
● Undergoes nodular hyperplasia
● Compresses the prostatic urethra leading to obstructive symptoms

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) enters the systemic circulation during malignancy.
back:
● PSA is a serine protease produced by prostatic epithelium
● Normally stays in lumina; leaks into blood capillaries via stroma when glandular architecture is disrupted by cancer or inflammation

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the diagnostic findings of a hard, irregular nodule in the Peripheral Zone with the smooth enlargement of the Transition Zone.
back:
● Peripheral Zone Nodule: Suggestive of Adenocarcinoma (80% of cases)
● Transition Zone Enlargement: Characteristic of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the specific stromal component responsible for the expulsion of prostatic fluid into the urethra during ejaculation.
back:
● Smooth muscle fibers
● Embedded in dense fibromuscular stroma
● Contracts forcefully under sympathetic stimulation

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The majority of prostatic glandular tissue (~70%), which is the most frequent site for adenocarcinoma development, is the [___].
back:
● Peripheral Zone
● Contains the 'Main Glands'
● Located posteriorly; easily palpable via digital rectal exam

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A patient’s biopsy shows glandular hyperplasia and stromal proliferation. If these changes are localized to the mucosal glands, which zone is being sampled?
back:
● Transition Zone
● Site of mucosal glands
● Site of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the histological organization of the prostate that allows it to store and then rapidly release secretions.
back:
● Tubuloacinar glands store secretions in wide lumina
● Surrounded by fibromuscular stroma (collagen, elastic, and smooth muscle) for rapid contractile release

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the Central Zone with the Transition Zone regarding their percentage of total prostatic volume and their gland types.
back:
● Central Zone: ~25% volume; contains submucosal glands
● Transition Zone: ~5% volume; contains mucosal glands

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the acidophilic, lamellated concretions found in the acini of elderly men that represent condensed glycoproteins.
back:
● Corpora amylacea
● Also called prostatic concretions
● Number increases with age; may calcify

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The prostatic zone that comprises only about 5% of glandular volume in young males but is the primary site for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia is the [___].
back:
• Transition zone.
• Contains mucosal glands.
• Hyperplasia leads to urethral obstruction.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 70-year-old male presents with a hard, irregular nodule felt during a digital rectal examination. Statistically, this malignancy most likely originated in which specific prostatic zone?
back:
• Peripheral zone.
• Site of 80% of prostatic adenocarcinomas.
• Contains the 'main' prostatic glands.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Explain the role of the prostatic fibromuscular stroma during the process of ejaculation.
back:
• Forceful contraction of smooth muscle fibers.
• Expels stored prostatic fluid into the urethra.
• Becomes part of the seminal fluid.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the Transition Zone and Peripheral Zone regarding their relative glandular volume and primary associated clinical pathologies.
back:
• Transition Zone: 5% volume; associated with BPH.
• Peripheral Zone: 70% volume; associated with adenocarcinoma.
• PZ is the largest zone; TZ is the smallest.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the composition and microscopic appearance of corpora amylacea found within prostatic acini.
back:
• Calcified glycoproteins/secretory material.
• Acidophilic, concentric lamellae.
• Diameter: 250 µm to 2 mm.
• Number increases with age.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The largest glandular zone of the prostate is deficient anteriorly, where it is replaced by a thick layer of [___].
back:
• Anterior fibromuscular stroma.
• Non-glandular component.
• Consists of collagen, elastic, and smooth muscle fibers.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A patient presents with pelvic pain and a significantly elevated serum Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA). Identify the two major underlying pathologies indicated by this biomarker.
back:
• Prostatitis (Acute or Chronic).
• Prostatic Cancer (Adenocarcinoma).
• PSA is a serine protease leaked from stroma.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Detail the mechanism of ductal drainage for the 'main glands' of the peripheral zone compared to the 'mucosal glands' of the transition zone.
back:
• Mucosal glands: Open directly into prostatic urethra.
• Main glands: Long ducts passing through central/transition zones.
• Submucosal glands: Drain through the transition zone.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Distinguish between the glands found in the Central Zone and the Transition Zone of the prostate.
back:
• Central Zone: Submucosal glands; 25% volume.
• Transition Zone: Mucosal glands; 5% volume.
• Both zones surround the prostatic urethra.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: List the three concentric glandular zones of the prostate and their approximate volume percentages in young males.
back:
• Transition Zone (5%).
• Central Zone (25%).
• Peripheral Zone (70%).

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The [___] zone of the prostate gland is the primary site for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH), leading to urethral compression.
back:
* Transition zone.
* Comprises approximately 5% of prostatic volume in young men.
* Contains mucosal glands that open directly into the prostatic urethra.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 70-year-old male presents with difficulty initiating urination and a weak stream. Digital rectal exam confirms nodular enlargement. Hyperplasia in this condition is most prominent in the [___] zone.
back:
* Transition Zone.
* BPH causes urethral obstruction due to its proximity to the prostatic urethra.
* Characterized by hyperplasia of both glands and fibromuscular stroma.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which the prostatic fibromuscular stroma contributes to the expulsion of prostatic fluid.
back:
* Contains abundant smooth muscle fibers interspersed with collagen.
* Contracts forcefully under sympathetic stimulation during ejaculation.
* Compresses tubuloacinar glands to release stored secretions into the urethra.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the peripheral zone and transition zone of the prostate regarding their common associated clinical pathologies.
back:
* Peripheral Zone: Outermost region (70% volume); primary site for 80% of prostatic adenocarcinomas.
* Transition Zone: Innermost region (5% volume); primary site for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Name the specific enzymes in prostatic fluid responsible for the slow liquefaction of coagulated semen in the vagina.
back:
* Fibrinolysin.
* Serine protease (Prostate-specific antigen/PSA).
* These enzymes dissolve the fibrinogen-based clot formed by seminal vesicle secretions.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Small, acidophilic, lamellated bodies found within the lumens of prostatic acini that increase with age are termed [___].
back:
* Corpora amylacea (Prostatic concretions).
* Formed by glycoprotein condensation around cell fragments.
* Often become partially calcified in elderly patients.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 65-year-old man presents with elevated PSA levels. If a needle biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma, identify the prostatic zone where the malignancy most likely originated.
back:
* Peripheral Zone.
* Contains the main prostatic glands.
* This outermost region is the most common site for prostatic cancer development.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the relationship between the anatomical location of the transition zone and the obstructive symptoms seen in BPH.
back:
* Surrounds the proximal portion of the prostatic urethra.
* Hyperplasia in this small volume causes rapid inward compression.
* Manifests as urinary hesitancy, weak stream, and incomplete emptying.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Distinguish the three concentric zones of the prostate based on the types of glands they contain.
back:
* Transition Zone: Mucosal glands.
* Central Zone: Submucosal glands.
* Peripheral Zone: Main glands (constituting 70% of total glandular tissue).

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Specify the histological composition and anatomical location of the anterior fibromuscular stroma.
back:
* Located where the peripheral zone is deficient anteriorly.
* Composed of dense irregular connective tissue and smooth muscle.
* Lacks glandular (secretory) elements entirely.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) primarily involves the [___] zone of the prostate, leading to the clinical compression of the prostatic urethra.
back: • Transition zone • Contains the mucosal glands • Primary site for the development of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) • Pathologically compresses the proximal urethra leading to urinary symptoms.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 65-year-old male presents with a hard, irregular nodule felt on the posterior aspect of the prostate during rectal examination. This pathology most likely originated in the [___].
back: • Peripheral zone • Primary site for approximately 80% of prostatic adenocarcinomas • Largest zone comprising 70% of glandular tissue • Located posteriorly and most susceptible to digital rectal examination.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Explain the physiological role and clinical significance of elevated serum Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) levels.
back: • PSA is a serine protease enzyme secreted by prostatic epithelium • It normally facilitates the liquefaction of the seminal clot • High serum levels indicate architectural damage from prostatitis or adenocarcinoma.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Contrast the anatomical location and primary associated pathology of the Transition Zone versus the Peripheral Zone.
back: • Transition Zone: Innermost zone surrounding the urethra; site of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) • Peripheral Zone: Outermost posterior zone; site of 80% of Prostatic Adenocarcinomas • Associated with different gland types.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Identify the acidophilic, lamellated bodies frequently found in the acini of an aging prostate gland.
back: • Corpora amylacea (prostatic concretions) • Represent calcified condensations of secretory glycoproteins and cell fragments • Their prevalence increases significantly with age • Found within the lumina of the tubuloacinar glands.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: The [___] zone of the prostate constitutes approximately 70% of the glandular tissue and contains the 'main glands' whose ducts are notably long.
back: • Peripheral zone • Most susceptible to malignancy (adenocarcinoma) • Ducts pass through the central and transition zones • Deficient anteriorly where it is replaced by fibromuscular stroma.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: A 55-year-old male reports a weak urinary stream and hesitancy. Histology shows nodular hyperplasia of mucosal glands and fibromuscular stroma. Name the specific zone affected.
back: • Transition zone of the prostate • Anatomical site specifically involved in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) • Surrounds the proximal prostatic urethra • Represents 5% of total volume in young males.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Describe the specific role of prostatic fibrinolysin and serine protease in male reproductive physiology.
back: • Secreted into the prostatic fluid • These enzymes facilitate the slow liquefaction of the seminal coagulum • This process occurs after ejaculation into the vagina • Essential for promoting sperm motility.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Distinguish between the mucosal, submucosal, and main glands of the prostate based on their specific zonal distribution.
back: • Mucosal glands: Transition zone (innermost) • Submucosal glands: Central zone (middle) • Main glands: Peripheral zone (outermost) • All types eventually drain their secretions into the prostatic urethra.

category: Describe the lobes of prostate and correlate with the pathologies of prostate
front: Characterize the histological composition of the prostatic stroma and its functional significance during ejaculation.
back: • Dense fibromuscular stroma • Contains collagen fibers, elastic fibers, and abundant smooth muscle cells • Contracts forcefully during ejaculation to release stored glandular secretions into the prostatic urethra.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The outermost surface of the ovary is lined by a layer of simple cuboidal epithelium known as the [___].
back:
- Germinal (surface) epithelium
- Rests on the tunica albuginea
- Continuous with the mesothelium of the mesovarium

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 24-year-old female presents with hirsutism, acne, and irregular menses. Ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries with multiple subcapsular cysts. Histological diagnosis is [___].
back:
- Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
- Elevated LH causes increased androgen production
- Characterized by failure of follicles to reach maturity/ovulation

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain the mechanism by which the theca interna contributes to estrogen synthesis during the follicular phase.
back:
- Theca cells secrete androstenedione
- Steroid precursor diffuses across basement membrane to granulosa cells
- Converted to 17β-estradiol via aromatase enzyme

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: In a histological section of the corpus luteum, distinguish between Granulosa Lutein and Theca Lutein cells based on morphology.
back:
- Granulosa Lutein: Large (30 µm), pale-staining, 80% of volume
- Theca Lutein: Smaller (15 µm), dark-staining, peripherally located

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the structural components typically found within the ovarian medulla.
back:
- Loose connective tissue core
- Abundant large, coiled blood vessels
- Lymphatic vessels and nerves

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A histological section shows a primary oocyte arrested in prophase I, surrounded by a single layer of flattened, squamous cells, identifying it as a [___] follicle.
back:
- Primordial follicle
- Located in the most superficial cortex
- Most numerous follicle type at birth

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Biopsy of an ovary reveals multiple collapsing follicles with apoptotic granulosa cells and autolyzed oocytes. Name the physiological process occurring.
back:
- Follicular Atresia
- Can occur at any stage of development
- Characterized by macrophage-mediated disposal of remnants

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Describe the transition from a primary to a secondary follicle focusing on the formation of the antrum.
back:
- Appearance of intercellular clefts between granulosa cells
- Accumulation of liquor folliculi
- Clefts coalesce into a single crescent-shaped cavity (Antrum)

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the histological appearance of a Graafian follicle versus a Secondary follicle.
back:
- Graafian: Large cystic structure (2-3 cm) bulging at surface; thinner stratum granulosum
- Secondary: Smaller; presence of an early antrum and cumulus oophorus

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the end-stage histological structure formed after the involution and fibrosis of the corpus luteum.
back:
- Corpus albicans
- Dense mass of white fibrous/collagenous tissue
- Formed due to drop in progesterone/LH

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The surface of the ovary is covered by a specialized layer of simple cuboidal cells known as the [___] epithelium.
back: * Germinal epithelium. * Misnamed as it does not give rise to germ cells. * Located superficial to the dense fibrous tunica albuginea.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 24-year-old female presents with hirsutism, acne, and infertility. Ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries with multiple subcapsular cysts. Histologically, these cysts represent an arrest in the maturation of [___].
back: * Growing ovarian follicles. * Persistent elevated LH levels lead to increased androgen production. * Failure of any single follicle to reach the Graafian stage.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain how theca interna cells contribute to the synthesis of the most potent female estrogen.
back: * Transform from stromal cells into steroid-producing cells. * Secrete androstenedione under LH influence. * Androstenedione is converted to estradiol by granulosa cells.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the light microscopic appearance of granulosa lutein cells with theca lutein cells within the corpus luteum.
back: * Granulosa Lutein: Large (30um), pale-staining, central mass. * Theca Lutein: Smaller (15um), darkly-staining, located at the periphery or along septa. * Both contain yellowish lutein pigment.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Describe the histological characteristics and primary function of the zona pellucida.
back: * Acidophilic, homogeneous layer between the oocyte and granulosa cells. * Composed of glycoproteins ZP1-ZP4. * Functions as a sperm receptor and barrier to polyspermy.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: In a primordial follicle, the primary oocyte is immediately surrounded by a single layer of [___] follicular cells.
back: * Squamous (flattened). * Follicular cells are attached to each other by desmosomes. * Resting on a basal lamina separating them from the ovarian stroma.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A biopsy shows follicles with apoptotic granulosa cells, autolyzed ova, and collapsed zona pellucidae. Identify this physiological process.
back: * Follicular atresia. * Occurs in most follicles that begin growth during a cycle. * Remnants are phagocytosed by macrophages in the stroma.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain the mechanical role of the theca externa during the process of ovulation.
back: * Outermost layer of the theca folliculi. * Composed of smooth muscle cells and collagen fibers. * Muscle contraction helps rupture the Graafian follicle to release the oocyte.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Distinguish between the ovarian cortex and the ovarian medulla based on their light microscopic components.
back: * Cortex: Richly cellular stroma with spindle-shaped cells and scattered ovarian follicles. * Medulla: Central loose connective tissue containing prominent blood vessels, lymphatics, and nerves.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the histological fate of the corpus luteum following the cessation of progesterone secretion if fertilization fails.
back: * Undergoes autolysis of lutein cells. * Replaced by a mass of white fibrous connective tissue. * Forms the corpus albicans (white body).

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The surface of the ovary is covered by a layer of simple cuboidal epithelium historically referred to as the [___].
back:
• Germinal epithelium (or surface epithelium).
• It is continuous with the mesothelium of the mesovarium.
• Beneath it lies the tunica albuginea.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 22-year-old female presents with irregular menses and hirsutism. Ultrasound reveals enlarged ovaries with multiple subcapsular cysts. This condition is characterized by follicles failing to mature, a diagnosis known as [___].
back:
• Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).
• Pathophysiology: Elevated LH levels leads to increased androgen production.
• Histology: Absence of mature Graafian follicles and corpora lutea.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain the role of theca interna cells in the synthesis of ovarian hormones during the follicular phase.
back:
• Synthesize androstenedione (androgen) under LH stimulation.
• These cells exhibit features of steroid-secreting cells (abundant SER, tubular cristae).
• Transfer androgens to granulosa cells for conversion into estrogen.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the microscopic luminal appearance of a multilaminar primary follicle with that of a secondary (antral) follicle.
back:
• Multilaminar Primary: A solid mass (stratum granulosum) with no internal cavity.
• Secondary: Contains a crescent-shaped cavity called the antrum folliculi filled with liquor folliculi.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the primary hormone secreted by the granulosa lutein cells of the corpus luteum and its main cytological feature.
back:
• Hormone: Progesterone.
• Feature: Large cells (30 µm) with pale-staining cytoplasm containing lutein pigment.
• Function: Prepares the endometrium for implantation.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The acidophilic, glycoprotein-rich layer that first appears in the unilaminar primary follicle to separate the oocyte from follicular cells is the [___].
back:
• Zona pellucida.
• Secreted by the oocyte.
• Contains ZP receptors required for sperm-oocyte binding during fertilization.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A biopsy specimen shows a dense mass of white fibrous connective tissue in the ovarian cortex. Explain the origin of this structure.
back:
• It is a Corpus Albicans.
• Formed by the involution and fibrosis of a non-fertilized corpus luteum.
• Represents the end-stage of follicular regression.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Describe the 'Two-Cell Theory' regarding the production of 17β-estradiol within the ovarian follicle.
back:
• LH stimulates theca interna to produce androstenedione.
• Androstenedione diffuses into granulosa cells.
• FSH stimulates granulosa cells to aromatize the androgen into 17β-estradiol.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the light microscopic features of granulosa lutein cells versus theca lutein cells in terms of size and location.
back:
• Granulosa Lutein: Large (30 µm), central location, make up 80% of the corpus luteum.
• Theca Lutein: Smaller (15 µm), peripheral location or along septa, stain more intensely.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Which specific histological zone of the ovary contains the hilus cells and large coiled blood vessels, but lacks ovarian follicles?
back:
• Ovarian Medulla.
• Composition: Loose connective tissue, rich vascular plexuses, lymphatics, and nerves.
• Lacks the follicles characteristic of the cortex.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The outermost covering of the ovary, historically known as the germinal epithelium, consists of a single layer of [___] epithelium.
back:
• Simple cuboidal epithelium
• Rests on a basement membrane
• Continuous with the mesothelium of the mesovarium

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 24-year-old female presents with infertility, acne, and hirsutism. Ultrasound reveals enlarged ovaries with multiple subepithelial cysts. This clinical condition, driven by elevated LH and androgen production, is [___].
back:
• Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
• Characterized by failure of follicular maturation
• Multiple follicular cysts reflect arrested growth stages

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain the role of theca interna cells in estrogen synthesis within a growing ovarian follicle.
back:
• Secrete the steroid androstenedione
• Androstenedione passes to granulosa cells
• Granulosa cells convert it into 17β-estradiol via aromatase

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Distinguish between a primordial follicle and a unilaminar primary follicle based on their follicular cell morphology.
back:
• Primordial: Single layer of flat (squamous) follicular cells
• Unilaminar Primary: Single layer of cuboidal follicular cells
• Both surround a primary oocyte

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Detail the primary histological constituents of the ovarian medulla.
back:
• Central zone of loose connective tissue
• Highly vascularized with abundant blood vessels
• Contains lymphatic vessels and nerves
• No distinct demarcation from the cortex

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The dense, fibrous connective tissue capsule located immediately beneath the ovarian surface epithelium is the [___].
back:
• Tunica albuginea
• Provides structural integrity to the ovary
• Located between the germinal epithelium and cortex

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Following ovulation, if fertilization does not occur, the corpus luteum eventually transforms into a white fibrous scar known as [___].
back:
• Corpus albicans
• Formed by autolysis of lutein cells
• Consists primarily of dense connective/fibrous tissue

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Describe the histological sequence of events during follicular atresia.
back:
• Follicular cell death by apoptosis
• Autolysis of the oocyte
• Collapse and thickening of the zona pellucida
• Disposal of remnants by macrophages

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the appearance and position of granulosa lutein cells versus theca lutein cells in the corpus luteum.
back:
• Granulosa Lutein: Large, pale-staining cells; 80% of population; centrally located
• Theca Lutein: Smaller, darker-staining cells; peripherally located or in septa

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the origin and light microscopic staining characteristic of the zona pellucida.
back:
• Origin: Secreted by the oocyte (ZP1-ZP4 glycoproteins)
• Staining: Deeply acidophilic (pink/red) in H&E sections
• Position: Between the oocyte and granulosa cells

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The surface of the ovary is covered by a layer of modified simple cuboidal epithelium known as [___].
back:
**Germinal (Surface) Epithelium**
* Cohesive layer of simple cuboidal cells.
* Rests on the underlying tunica albuginea.
* Continuous with the peritoneal mesothelium at the ovarian hilum.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 25-year-old female presents with irregular periods, acne, and hirsutism. LM of the ovary shows numerous subcapsular cysts which represent [___].
back:
**Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)**
* Multiple growing follicles fail to reach full maturity.
* Absence of ovulation leads to follicular cyst formation.
* Characterized by an thickened tunica albuginea and stromal hyperplasia.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain the histological transformation of follicular cells when a primordial follicle develops into a unilaminar primary follicle.
back:
**Follicular Activation**
* Flat squamous follicular cells differentiate into cuboidal cells.
* The oocyte enlarges to approximately 120 μm.
* Formation of the acidophilic Zona Pellucida begins.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the histological structure of the theca interna with that of the theca externa in a mature follicle.
back:
**Theca Folliculi Differentiation**
* **Theca Interna:** Inner vascular layer; contains cuboidal steroid-producing cells (secrete androstenedione).
* **Theca Externa:** Outer fibrous layer; contains smooth muscle cells and collagen fibers.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the characteristic fluid-filled space that distinguishes a secondary follicle from a primary follicle.
back:
**Antrum (Antrum Folliculi)**
* Small intercellular clefts filled with liquor folliculi coalesce.
* Forms a single crescent-shaped cavity.
* Presence marks the transition to the antral stage.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The central zone of the ovary, composed of loose connective tissue, large blood vessels, and nerves, is termed the [___].
back:
**Ovarian Medulla**
* Lacks ovarian follicles.
* Richly supplied with tortuous blood and lymphatic vessels.
* Merges with the cortex without a distinct line of demarcation.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 30-year-old female undergoes a biopsy after a non-fertilized cycle; a white, scar-like mass of dense collagenous tissue is noted. Identify the structure.
back:
**Corpus Albicans**
* Formed by the involution of the corpus luteum.
* Lutein cells undergo autolysis.
* Replaced by white fibrous connective tissue.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Describe the histological composition of the Corpus Luteum's two distinct endocrine cell populations.
back:
**Lutein Cells**
* **Granulosa Lutein (80%):** Large, pale cells; secrete progesterone and estradiol.
* **Theca Lutein:** Smaller, darker-staining cells at the periphery; secrete androstenedione.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Distinguish between the Cumulus Oophorus and the Corona Radiata in a Graafian follicle.
back:
**Oocyte Support Structures**
* **Cumulus Oophorus:** The heap of granulosa cells anchoring the oocyte to the wall.
* **Corona Radiata:** The single layer of columnar granulosa cells directly surrounding the oocyte.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the protective, acidophilic glycoprotein layer secreted between the oocyte and the granulosa cells.
back:
**Zona Pellucida**
* 5–10 μm thick homogeneous layer.
* Contains ZP1, ZP2, ZP3, and ZP4 proteins.
* Facilitates sperm binding and prevents polyspermy via cortical granules.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: The outermost covering of the ovary, despite its historical name, consists of a single layer of simple cuboidal epithelium known as the [___].
back:
• Surface epithelium (Germinal epithelium).
• Lies above the tunica albuginea.
• Continuous with the mesothelium of the mesovarium.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A histological section of an ovary from a woman of reproductive age reveals a large, cystic structure measuring 2 cm that bulges the ovarian surface. This structure is a [___].
back:
• Mature (Graafian) follicle.
• Characterized by a massive antrum.
• Reaches full cortical thickness before ovulation.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Describe the histological organization of the ovarian theca folliculi during the transition to a multilaminar primary follicle.
back:
• Theca Interna: Highly vascular, cuboidal secretory cells (steroid-producing).
• Theca Externa: Outer fibrous layer with fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells.
• Separated from granulosa cells by a basement membrane.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Contrast the light microscopic appearance of Granulosa Lutein cells versus Theca Lutein cells within the corpus luteum.
back:
• Granulosa Lutein: Large (30 µm), pale-staining, central location; makes up 80% of the gland.
• Theca Lutein: Smaller (15 µm), darker-staining, located peripherally or along septa.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the deep acidophilic, homogeneous band located between the oocyte and the stratum granulosum in growing follicles.
back:
• Zona Pellucida.
• Composed of four glycoproteins (ZP1-ZP4).
• Secreted by the oocyte; involved in sperm binding.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: In the ovarian cortex, follicles consisting of a primary oocyte surrounded by only a single layer of flattened epithelial cells are classified as [___] follicles.
back:
• Primordial follicles.
• Most abundant type in the cortex.
• Arrested in prophase of Meiosis I.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: A 28-year-old female presents with infertility. Histology of the ovary shows multiple subcapsular cysts and a thickened tunica albuginea, but lacks a corpus luteum. This indicates a failure of [___].
back:
• Ovulation.
• Characteristic of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).
• Linked to elevated LH and androgen levels.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Explain the process of 'Antrum' formation as a follicle transitions from primary to secondary stage.
back:
• Intercellular clefts appear in the stratum granulosum.
• Clefts fill with liquor folliculi (plasma exudate + granulosa secretions).
• Clefts coalesce into a single, crescent-shaped cavity.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Distinguish between the light microscopic composition of the ovarian cortex and the ovarian medulla.
back:
• Cortex: Outer zone; compact stroma with spindle cells and follicles.
• Medulla: Inner core; loose connective tissue with large convoluted blood vessels and nerves.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovaries
front: Identify the histological remnant that appears as a wavy, white mass of fibrous connective tissue following the regression of the corpus luteum.
back:
• Corpus Albicans.
• Formed by autolysis of lutein cells.
• Eventually disappears or remains as a small scar.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: The most immature ovarian follicles, found in the ovarian cortex of a female child, consist of a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of [___] follicular cells.
back:
• Flattened (squamous) epithelial cells.
• Attached to each other by desmosomes.
• Rest on a thin basal lamina.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 24-year-old female presents with hirsutism and irregular periods. Ultrasound shows multiple small cystic structures in the subcapsular region. These 'cysts' represent [___].
back:
• Growing follicles that failed to reach maturity.
• Degenerating follicles associated with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).
• Chronic lack of ovulation due to elevated LH.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Describe the origin and light microscopic appearance of the zona pellucida as it first appears in a unilaminar primary follicle.
back:
• Secreted by the maturing oocyte.
• Appears as a deeply acidophilic, amorphous layer.
• Contains ZP1-ZP4 glycoproteins for sperm recognition.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the histological transition from a multilaminar primary follicle to a secondary follicle regarding luminal morphology.
back:
• Multilaminar: Preantral; consists of solid layers of stratum granulosum.
• Secondary: Antral; contains fluid-filled spaces that coalesce into a crescent-shaped cavity.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Identify the steroid-producing layer of the theca folliculi that contains fenestrated capillaries and secretes androstenedione.
back:
• Theca interna.
• Composed of cuboidal secretory cells.
• Precursor is converted to estradiol by granulosa cells.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: In a secondary follicle, the specific group of granulosa cells that immediately surrounds the oocyte and radiates outward is called the [___].
back:
• Corona radiata.
• Projects into the antrum within the cumulus oophorus.
• Remains with oocyte during ovulation.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A histological section shows a large (2-3 cm) cystic structure with a thinned stratum granulosum and a massive fluid-filled cavity. Diagnosis?
back:
• Mature (Graafian) follicle.
• Represents the pre-ovulatory stage.
• Characterized by maximum accumulation of liquor folliculi.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Explain the role of theca externa smooth muscle cells during the mid-cycle hormonal surge.
back:
• Contraction helps facilitate the rupture of the Graafian follicle.
• Assists in the physical release of the oocyte (ovulation).
• Outer layer of the theca folliculi.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Distinguish between granulosa lutein and theca lutein cells within a freshly formed corpus luteum.
back:
• Granulosa Lutein: Large (30μm), pale, central (80% of mass).
• Theca Lutein: Smaller (15μm), dark-staining, peripheral or along septa.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Name the remnant white fibrous mass formed when the corpus luteum undergoes involution if fertilization fails.
back:
• Corpus albicans.
• Composed of white fibrous connective tissue.
• Formed by autolysis of lutein cells and collagenization.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: The [___] follicle, the earliest stage found in the ovarian cortex of a female child, consists of a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of flattened epithelial cells.
back:
• Primordial Follicle
• Contains oocyte arrested in Prophase I
• Follicular cells are squamous
• Rests on a basal lamina

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 24-year-old female presents with irregular periods and hirsutism. Histological examination of an ovary would likely reveal multiple peripheral cysts, which are actually [___] that failed to ovulate.
back:
• Growing Ovarian Follicles
• Characteristic of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
• Failed maturation due to elevated LH and androgens

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Explain the steroidogenic collaboration between the theca interna and granulosa cells in a multilaminar primary follicle.
back:
• Theca interna: Secretes androstenedione (androgen)
• Granulosa cells: Convert androstenedione to 17-beta estradiol
• Stimulated by FSH and LH

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the structural arrangement of the oocyte in a secondary (antral) follicle versus a mature Graafian follicle.
back:
• Secondary: Small antral clefts coalesce; oocyte in cumulus oophorus
• Graafian: Huge, crescentic antrum; thinned stratum granulosum; bulges on ovarian surface

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Identify the primary hormone secreted by granulosa lutein cells and the specific enzyme required for their estrogen production.
back:
• Progesterone (main product)
• Aromatase (converts thecal androgens to estradiol)
• Comprise 80% of corpus luteum

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: The deeply acidophilic, homogeneous layer appearing between the oocyte and cuboidal granulosa cells in a unilaminar primary follicle is the [___].
back:
• Zona Pellucida
• Composed of glycoproteins ZP1, ZP2, ZP3, ZP4
• Secreted by the oocyte
• Functions as a sperm receptor site

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A patient is observed to have a white, scar-like fibrous mass in the ovarian cortex 14 days after a non-fertile cycle. This structure is the [___].
back:
• Corpus Albicans
• Formed by autolysis of lutein cells
• Represents the degenerated corpus luteum
• Rich in collagenous connective tissue

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Describe the histological transition of follicular cells during the transformation from a primordial to a unilaminar primary follicle.
back:
• Change from squamous to cuboidal shape
• Proliferation via mitotic division
• Formation of gap junctions (maculae communicantes)

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Distinguish between the theca interna and theca externa of a multilaminar follicle regarding cell type and function.
back:
• Theca Interna: Cuboidal steroid-secreting cells; rich capillary network
• Theca Externa: Fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells; aids in ovulation

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Specify the hallmark light microscopic feature that defines the transition from a primary to a secondary follicle.
back:
• Antrum Folliculi
• Fluid-filled cavity (liquor folliculi)
• Formation of the cumulus oophorus and corona radiata

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A primordial follicle is histologically characterized by a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of [___] follicular cells.
back:
- Flattened (squamous) follicular cells
- Rests on a basal lamina
- Oocyte is arrested in prophase of meiosis I

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 24-year-old female presents with irregular periods and hirsutism. Ultrasound reveals multiple small subcapsular cysts. Histologically, these cysts represent [___] that failed to reach full maturity.
back:
- Growing ovarian follicles (PCOS)
- Arrested development before ovulation
- Associated with thickened theca interna

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Explain the biological cooperation between theca interna and granulosa cells in estrogen synthesis.
back:
- Theca interna: Secretes androstenedione
- Granulosa cells: Convert androstenedione to 17β-estradiol via aromatase
- Facilitated by FSH and LH

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the histological appearance of a secondary (antral) follicle with a mature Graafian follicle.
back:
- Secondary: Small, crescent-shaped intercellular clefts (antrum)
- Graafian: Single, huge follicular cavity; bulges on ovarian surface
- Size: Graafian measures 2–3 cm

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Identify the acidophilic, glycoprotein-rich layer that appears between the oocyte and granulosa cells during the unilaminar primary stage.
back:
- Zona Pellucida
- Contains ZP1, ZP2, ZP3, and ZP4
- Functions as a sperm receptor barrier

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: During the transition from a primordial follicle to a unilaminar primary follicle, the follicular cells undergo a morphologic change from squamous to [___].
back:
- Simple cuboidal epithelium
- Oocyte size increases to ~120 μm
- Gap junctions (maculae communicantes) develop

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Following ovulation, a patient's biopsy shows a collapsed follicle filled with large, pale-staining cells containing lutein pigment. Name the two cell types present.
back:
- Granulosa lutein cells (80%, large/pale)
- Theca lutein cells (Small, dark, peripheral)
- Primary function: Progesterone secretion

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Describe the formation and contents of the antrum folliculi during the secondary follicle stage.
back:
- Intercellular clefts coalesce into a single cavity
- Filled with Liquor Folliculi
- Contains: Hyaluronic acid, fibrinogen, and high steroid concentrations

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the theca interna and theca externa layers in a multilaminar primary follicle.
back:
- Theca Interna: Cuboidal secretory cells (steroidogenic), fenestrated capillaries
- Theca Externa: Smooth muscle cells, fibroblasts, collagen fibers
- Divided by a basement membrane from granulosa

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Identify the specific cluster of granulosa cells that projects into the antrum and the radiating layer immediately surrounding the oocyte.
back:
- Cumulus Oophorus (the heap/mound)
- Corona Radiata (the radiating outer layer)
- Attached to oocyte via filopodia

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: In the ovarian cortex, a primordial follicle is histologically identified by a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of [___] follicular cells.
back:
• Flattened (squamous) epithelial cells.
• Attached to each other by desmosomes.
• Rest on a thin basal lamina.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 22-year-old female presents with irregular cycles and hirsutism. Ultrasound reveals multiple small peripheral cysts. Histologically, these represent arrested [___] follicles.
back:
• Growing (Secondary/Antral) follicles.
• Characteristic failure to reach full Graafian maturity.
• Result of elevated LH and androgen levels (PCOS).

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Explain the transition from a unilaminar primary follicle to a multilaminar primary follicle under light microscopy.
back:
• Granulosa cells proliferate into multiple layers (stratum granulosum).
• The surrounding stroma organizes into the theca folliculi.
• A well-defined basement membrane separates granulosa and theca layers.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the histological appearance of Granulosa Lutein cells with Theca Lutein cells within a mature corpus luteum.
back:
• Granulosa Lutein: Large (30 µm), pale-staining, central (80% of mass).
• Theca Lutein: Small (15 µm), dark-staining, peripheral or along septa.
• Both contain lipid droplets and lutein pigment.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Identify the steroid-producing layer of a growing follicle that is characterized by a rich network of fenestrated capillaries and cells with tubular mitochondrial cristae.
back:
• Theca interna.
• Derived from transformed stromal cells.
• Secretes androstenedione (converted to estradiol by granulosa cells).

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: The acidophilic, homogeneous layer found between the oocyte and granulosa cells in primary follicles is the [___].
back:
• Zona pellucida.
• Composed of glycoproteins ZP1, ZP2, ZP3, and ZP4.
• Secreted by the oocyte.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A pathologist observes a follicle with a crescent-shaped cavity filled with liquor folliculi. The oocyte is pushed to the side within a heap of cells called the [___].
back:
• Cumulus oophorus.
• Characteristic of a Secondary (Antral) follicle.
• Outermost layer of these cells is the Corona Radiata.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Describe the structural features that distinguish a Mature (Graafian) follicle from a Secondary follicle.
back:
• Huge antrum (2-3 cm diameter).
• Follicle spans the entire width of the ovarian cortex.
• Stratum granulosum becomes thin as cells cease dividing.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the fate of the corpus luteum if fertilization occurs versus if it does not occur.
back:
• Fertilization: Becomes Corpus Luteum of Pregnancy (persists ~6 months).
• No Fertilization: Degenerates after 10-14 days.
• Final remnant: Corpus albicans (white fibrous scar).

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: State the light microscopic appearance of the 'Corpus Albicans' in the ovarian stroma.
back:
• Dense mass of white fibrous connective tissue.
• Formed by autolysis of lutein cells.
• Replaces the degenerated corpus luteum.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: In the most immature stage of follicular development, the primordial follicle is characterized by a primary oocyte enveloped by a single layer of [___] follicular cells.
back:
• Flattened (squamous) epithelial cells
• Cells are attached to each other by desmosomes
• Entire follicle rests on a basal lamina separating it from the ovarian stroma

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 28-year-old female undergoes an ovarian biopsy which reveals follicles characterized by a large, single, crescent-shaped cavity filled with liquor folliculi and an oocyte shifted to one side. Identify this cavity and the corresponding follicular stage.
back:
• Cavity: Antrum (Antrum folliculi)
• Stage: Secondary (Antral) follicle
• Oocyte is located within a heap of granulosa cells called the cumulus oophorus

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Ovarian follicles characterized by a primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of flattened (squamous) follicular cells are called [___] follicles.
back:
• Primordial follicles.
• Located in the superficial ovarian cortex.
• Constitute the entire follicle population in childhood.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 24-year-old female presents with hirsutism and irregular cycles. Ultrasound reveals enlarged ovaries with numerous peripheral cysts. These cysts histologically represent [___].
back:
• Growing ovarian follicles.
• Arrested before reaching full maturity/ovulation.
• Characteristic of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Explain the role of theca interna cells during the follicular phase of the ovarian cycle.
back:
• Secretory cells that produce androstenedione.
• Androgen precursor is converted into estradiol by granulosa cells.
• Feature typical steroid-producing ultrastructure (abundant SER).

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: A 30-year-old female's ovarian biopsy shows a follicle with multiple layers of granulosa cells but NO fluid-filled cavity. This stage is identified as a [___].
back:
• Multilaminar primary follicle.
• Also known as a preantral follicle.
• Features a visible zona pellucida and developing theca folliculi.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Describe the specific arrangement of the 'corona radiata' in an antral follicle.
back:
• Single layer of radiating granulosa cells.
• Directly surrounds the primary oocyte.
• Situated immediately external to the zona pellucida.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: The acidophilic, amorphous layer containing glycoproteins ZP1-ZP4 located between the oocyte and follicular cells is the [___].
back:
• Zona pellucida.
• Appears during the primary follicle stage.
• Provides receptors for sperm binding during fertilization.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Histological examination of an ovary post-ovulation reveals a large, folded structure containing pale-staining, lipid-rich cells and a central blood clot. Name this structure.
back:
• Corpus luteum.
• Composed of granulosa lutein and theca lutein cells.
• Acts as a temporary endocrine organ producing progesterone.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Describe the morphological transition that characterizes the shift from a primary follicle to a secondary follicle.
back:
• Appearance of liquor-filled intercellular clefts within stratum granulosum.
• Coalescence of clefts into a single crescentic antrum.
• Oocyte pushed to the side into cumulus oophorus.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Contrast the microscopic appearance of follicular cells in a primordial follicle versus a unilaminar primary follicle.
back:
• Primordial: Single layer of flat (squamous) cells.
• Unilaminar: Single layer of cuboidal cells.
• Transition is stimulated by FSH at puberty.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of ovarian follicles in different stages of menstrual cycle
front: Identify the largest stage of follicular development that produces a visible bulge on the ovarian surface.
back:
• Mature (Graafian) follicle.
• Measures 2-3 cm in diameter.
• Features a massive antrum and thinned stratum granulosum.

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: The duct of the epididymis is lined by a specialized [___] epithelium.
back: • Pseudostratified columnar epithelium • Consists of tall principal cells and small basal cells

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: A 25-year-old male presents with infertility. Histology of the epididymal duct shows atrophy of tall columnar cells. These cells are primarily responsible for the reabsorption of [___].
back: • Testicular fluid • Vital for concentrating spermatozoa • Phagocytosis of cellular debris

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: Explain the role of the principal cells in secreting glycolipids that act as decapacitation factors.
back: • Coat the sperm head cell membrane • Temporarily inhibit fertilizing capability • Protect sperm during storage in the epididymis

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: A biopsy reveals a duct with a wavy luminal outline and ciliated cells. Contrast this with the typical light microscopic appearance of the ductus epididymis.
back: • Epididymis: Smooth/even luminal contour • Ductuli Efferentes: Wavy/scalloped contour • Epididymis has pseudostratified epithelium with stereocilia

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: Detail the progressive transition of the muscularis organization from the head/body to the tail of the epididymis.
back: • Head/Body: Thin layer of circular smooth muscle • Tail: Thick, three-layered coat (inner longitudinal, middle circular, outer longitudinal)

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: The non-motile, long, branching microvilli located on the apical surface of epididymal principal cells are termed [___].
back: • Stereocilia • Function: Increase surface area for fluid absorption • Distinguishes the segment from ciliated segments

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: A male with chronic, untreated gonorrhea develops bilateral scrotal pain and subsequent azoospermia. Histology shows ductal fibrosis. Identify the likely anatomical structure involved.
back: • Ductus epididymis (chronic epididymitis) • Fibrosis leads to luminal blockage • Common cause of obstructive infertility

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: How do the principal cells differentiate their management of luminal content compared to the ciliated cells of the ductuli efferentes?
back: • Epididymis: Reabsorbs fluid via stereocilia and secretes glycolipids • Ductuli: Move fluid via cilia and reabsorb via microvilli

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: Contrast the regenerative role of the basal cells with the metabolic secretory loop of principal cells in the epididymal lining.
back: • Basal cells: Small, round reserve/stem cells resting on lamina • Principal cells: Tall columnar, perform fluid reabsorption and glycolipid secretion

category: Describe the light microscopic structure of Epididymis
front: Identify the three gross histological regions of the comma-shaped epididymis through which spermatozoa pass sequentially.
back: • Head (caput) • Body (corpus) • Tail (cauda)

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: In Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), the numerous ovarian "cysts" visible on imaging or gross specimen actually represent arrested [___].
back:
- Growing ovarian follicles
- These follicles fail to reach full maturity (Graafian stage)
- Results in a complete lack of ovulation (anovulation)

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: A 24-year-old female presents with infertility, hirsutism, and irregular menses. Histological examination of her ovaries would likely reveal a total lack of which specific post-ovulatory structure?
back:
- Corpus luteum
- Chronic anovulation prevents the transformation of follicles into this endocrine body
- Leads to deficient progesterone production

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Explain the role of Luteinizing Hormone (LH) in the pathogenesis of hirsutism and acne seen in PCOS patients.
back:
- Constantly elevated LH stimulates theca interna cells
- Leads to excessive production of androgens (androstenedione)
- High systemic androgens drive sebaceous gland activity and terminal hair growth

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Contrast the histological appearance of the ovarian cortex in a normal reproductive-age female versus one with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
back:
- Normal: Presence of follicles at all stages (primordial to Graafian) and corpora lutea
- PCOS: Multiple arrested subcapsular follicles; absent corpora lutea; often shows a thickened tunica albuginea

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Identify the primary anterior pituitary hormone that is chronically elevated in PCOS, driving increased ovarian androgen synthesis.
back:
- Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
- Acts on theca folliculi to increase steroidogenesis
- Disturbs the normal FSH:LH ratio required for maturation

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: The failure of follicles to progress into the [___] stage is the primary histological basis for infertility in PCOS.
back:
- Mature (Graafian) follicle
- Arrest occurs during the transition to the tertiary stage
- Prevents the LH surge from triggering oocyte release

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: A patient with PCOS undergoes ultrasound showing "bilateral ovarian enlargement." Histologically, what changes in the ovarian stroma contribute to this finding?
back:
- Hyperplastic, richly cellular cortical stroma
- Increased thickness of the collagenous tunica albuginea
- Hypertrophy of the theca interna layer in multiple follicles

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Describe the functional state of the theca interna cells in the arrested follicles of a PCOS patient.
back:
- Hyperactive and increased in volume
- Over-secrete androstenedione under high LH influence
- This androgen is the substrate for conversion into potent estrogens/testosterone

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Distinguish between a functional "cyst" in PCOS and a normal Secondary (Antral) follicle.
back:
- Secondary Follicle: Developing structure with a crescent antrum, progressing toward maturation
- PCOS "Cyst": Arrested growing follicle; usually sub-centimeter; lacks the potential for imminent ovulation

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: List three cutaneous manifestations of PCOS that serve as clinical evidence of underlying histological androgen excess.
back:
- Hirsutism (face/chest hair)
- Acne vulgaris
- Male-pattern alopecia (thinning of scalp hair)
- Acanthosis nigricans (often associated with insulin resistance)

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: In Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), the ovaries are characterized by constantly elevated levels of [___], which leads to increased ovarian androgen production.
back:
• Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
• High LH stimulates theca cells
• Results in hyperandrogenism

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: A 22-year-old female presents with primary infertility, severe acne, and hirsutism. Pelvic ultrasound shows bilateral enlarged ovaries with multiple subcapsular cystic structures. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
• Key findings: Hirsutism, anovulation, and polycystic morphology

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Explain the histological nature of the 'cysts' found in the ovaries of patients with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
back:
• They are not true cysts
• Represent growing ovarian follicles
• Arrested development; fail to reach mature (Graafian) stage

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Contrast the fate of a dominant follicle in a normal cycle with the follicular dynamics seen in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
back:
• Normal: One follicle becomes a mature Graafian follicle and ovulates
• PCOS: Multiple follicles begin growth but fail to mature or release an oocyte

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Identify the specific physiological event that fails to occur in PCOS, directly leading to the formation of multiple follicular cysts and infertility.
back:
• Ovulation
• Caused by failure of follicles to reach full maturity due to hormonal imbalance

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: The manifestation of growth of extra body hair on the face and chest in PCOS patients is histologically driven by the overactivity of [___] cells in the ovary.
back:
• Theca interna cells (or Theca cells)
• These cells secrete androstenedione/androgens under high LH stimulation

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: A patient with irregular menses is found to have high androgen levels. How does the histological state of the ovarian follicles in this condition contribute to her menstrual irregularity?
back:
• Lack of mature Graafian follicles means no ovulation
• No ovulation prevents the formation of a functional corpus luteum
• Results in progesterone deficiency and cycle disruption

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Describe the relationship between Luteinizing Hormone (LH) and the physical enlargement of the ovaries in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
back:
• Persistent high LH prevents the LH surge needed for ovulation
• Stimulates theca cell hyperplasia and androgen secretion
• Causes accumulation of multiple immature, fluid-filled follicles (enlargement)

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Distinguish between a 'Mature Graafian Follicle' and the 'Cysts' of PCOS based on their size and position in the ovarian cortex.
back:
• Graafian: Large (2-3 cm), extends full breadth of cortex, produces surface bulge
• PCOS Cysts: Smaller, numerous, usually arrested in the pre-antral or early antral stages

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: Specify the clinical term for the growth of extra body hair on the face and chest commonly seen as a manifestation of PCOS.
back:
• Hirsutism
• Results from increased androgen production by the hyperplastic theca cells

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: In Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), the numerous ovarian "cysts" observed grossly actually represent arrested [___] that fail to reach maturity.
back:
• Growing ovarian follicles
• These follicles are typically arrested at the pre-antral or early antral stage
• Failure to reach the Graafian stage prevents ovulation.

category: Describe the histological basis and manifestation of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
front: A 24-year-old female presents with infertility and hirsutism. Histological examination of her ovaries would likely show a thickened tunica albuginea and a total absence of [___].
back:
• Corpora lutea (Corpus luteum)
• Indicates chronic anovulation
